entry.title: A testbed game for studying self-governing groups of humans and AI agents
entry.summary: A Simulation Testbed for Self-Governing Human-Machine Institutions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces Megabike, a multi-agent simulator and serious game for studying whether mixed human-machine groups can govern themselves. Riders sharing a megabike must agree on steering, pedalling and resource distribution, and choose their political regime. In forty sessions with language-model riders, the agents chose regimes, elected leaders and expelled one another. The results show that different combinations of agent types can produce unexpected and counterproductive outcomes.

entry.title: Nothing Left Behind: Finding Evidence in Large Trial Collections
entry.summary: Nothing Left Behind: Embedding Retrieval and Language Model Screening for High Recall Evidence Search arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper compares two ways to find relevant evidence in a large collection: tagging items with labels and searching on them, versus using text embeddings to find candidates by meaning and then having a language model keep only the relevant ones. In a corpus of 7,354 randomized trials, label search found 45% of the evidence a systematic review would include, while the new approach found 92%. The authors propose a two-stage architecture that combines broad candidate retrieval with query-specific evidence filtering.

entry.title: Deep Bayesian Methods for Interpretable Nonlinear Structural System Identification
entry.summary: Deep Bayesian Filtering for Nonlinear Structural System Identification: A Tutorial on Structural and Physical Inductive Biases arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This tutorial systematically introduces deep Bayesian filtering for inferring mathematical models of nonlinear structural systems from measured data. It compares the Deep Markov Model, the Physics-guided Deep Markov Model (PgDMM), and the Neural Extended Kalman Filter (Neural EKF). The methods are evaluated on a three-dimensional shear-frame benchmark with hysteretic Bouc-Wen connections, covering dynamic state estimation and joint state and parameter estimation.

entry.title: FeatureLoop: Testing Coding Agents as Requirements Keep Changing
entry.summary: Benchmarking Coding Agents under Evolving Requirements arXiv · Oct 26, 2026FeatureLoop is a benchmark of 61 human-reviewed tasks drawn from 34 repositories, covering five primary programming languages and seven software forms. Tasks evolve through requirement-change feedback and completion feedback in a persistent workspace, and cumulative executable checks measure new behavior, repairs, and preservation of earlier functionality. Across 12 frontier models, the strongest completed 72.1% of tasks, but only 15.4% of observed failed stages recovered within two corrective revisions.

entry.title: Shared Context, Separate Engines: Concurrent Streaming Vision-Language Inference on Edge Chips
entry.summary: Shared Context, Separate Engines: Stateful Streaming Inference for Multimodal LLMs on Edge SoCs arXiv · Oct 26, 2026Edge SoCs combine CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, but current vision-language model runtimes usually run generation on one engine and leave the others idle. The paper presents \name, which separates each stream's versioned context from each engine's KV state so several heterogeneous accelerators can run stateful inference concurrently. The authors report higher throughput than the strongest single-engine baselines on Apple M4 Max, Rockchip RK3588, and Qualcomm QCS6490.

entry.title: GBClaw: An AI Agent Framework for Studying Grain Boundaries in Materials
entry.summary: Mechanistic discovery in grain boundary structure and deformation driven by agentic AI arXiv · Oct 21, 2026The paper introduces GBClaw, an agentic AI framework that uses large language models with specialized agents, tools, and memory to study how grain boundaries in materials are structured and deform. It was applied to 14 asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel, identifying various deformation modes. The results show that secondary misfit dislocations substantially change shear strength during boundary sliding.

entry.title: Long-wave infrared polarimetric image fusion to improve vehicle detection in remote sensing
entry.summary: PolMamba: Long-wave Infrared Polarimetric Remote Sensing Image Fusion for Vehicle Detection arXiv · Oct 19, 2026This paper addresses blurred vehicle contours and low contrast in infrared remote sensing images by proposing a Mamba-based model that fuses long-wave infrared total intensity with degree of linear polarization. It uses bidirectional state space scanning and prior-guided losses to reduce noise while keeping background structure and polarization features. The authors also release AIR-LWIR-Pol, a dataset of 1,901 registered image pairs. Using YOLO11, vehicle detection reaches 55.0% mAP50 and 29.4% mAP50-95, and the method outperforms comparison methods on four fusion metrics.

entry.title: Accelerated Dataflow: Scaling Efficient Inference in Streaming Data Analytics
entry.summary: Accelerated Dataflow: scaling inference in streaming data analytics with efficiency arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This paper presents a system on Google Cloud Dataflow for streaming pipelines that combine data processing with machine learning inference, such as large language model calls. It uses autoscaling co-designed for heterogeneous worker pools and prefix-aware batching. Compared with existing streaming data processing systems, the authors report 1.5x to 2x higher throughput at similar latency, up to 75% peak resource savings, and 84% lower peak tail latency. entry.title: A4-MR: Anatomy- and abnormality-aware MRI foundation model
entry.summary: A4-MR: Abnormality Aware Anatomical Alignment for MR arXiv · Oct 9, 2026This paper introduces A4-MR, a 3D vision-language foundation model trained on about 50,000 MRI studies, including roughly 491,000 series, with about half paired with radiology reports. It aims to learn anatomy localization, align image and text at the anatomical level, and represent healthy and abnormal anatomy distinctly. Across diverse downstream tasks, it outperforms existing foundation models, and with a frozen encoder it matches or exceeds task-specific segmentation models for knee and abdominal organ segmentation.

entry.title: NucShare: a lightweight framework sharing one decoder for nuclei segmentation
entry.summary: NucShare: Lightweight Nuclei Instance Segmentation with Foundation-Model Accuracy arXiv · Sep 28, 2026NucShare proposes a single U-Net-style decoder shared across three nuclei segmentation tasks, each with only a lightweight head, using 37% of the parameters of three independent decoders. A teacher model uses a UNI2-h encoder (690.5M parameters), while the student NucShare-S uses a ConvNeXt V2-Tiny encoder (34.7M parameters) and learns via output-level distillation. On PanNuke, the student keeps 99.1% of the teacher's mPQ (0.519), above CFR-SAM-H's 0.511, and runs 27.5 times faster per tile than the teacher.

entry.title: OpenESM: Energy-Steered Models as Scalable Foundation Learners
entry.summary: OpenEBFM: Energy-based Foundation Models Are Scalable Architecture arXiv · Oct 7, 2026This paper proposes energy-steered models (ESMs), a language modeling architecture that first refines a latent state over an energy landscape and then uses it to generate tokens. The authors pre-train ESMs on three large-scale corpora and evaluate them on 26 downstream tasks. They report promising scaling with model size and training data, and better results than GPT models on most tasks. The model weights and training infrastructure are publicly released.

entry.title: A differentiable watershed layer for trainable segmentation networks
entry.summary: The Power Watershed as a Differentiable Segmentation Layer arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper places a Power Watershed, the limit of a seeded Random Walker as its edge-weight exponent grows, at the end of a segmentation network so it can be trained end to end. The finite-exponent solve is exactly differentiable through one adjoint solve. On PanNuke nuclei segmentation, the layer turns a U-Net into an instance segmenter, raising instance F1 from 0.656 to 0.795. ★★★★ Notable: The authors embed a differentiable Power Watershed layer at the end of a U-Net and report instance F1 rising from 0.656 to 0.795 on PanNuke nuclei segmentation.

entry.title: Similar Scores, Opposite Failures: Human Correction for Video Caption Evaluation
entry.summary: Similar Scores, Opposite Failures: Human Correction as an Instrument for Video Caption Evaluation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper finds that reference-overlap metrics built for single-sentence image captions fail to separate reviewer-accepted from rejected dense video captions, performing near chance. Six frontier models captioned 196 short clips, which trained annotators post-edited against a fixed failure taxonomy, reviewing each caption once as a whole-clip overview and once window by window. entry.title: Predicting the Reward, Not the World: Training Models to Choose Better ML Programs
entry.summary: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes World Reward Models (WRMs) for search-based machine-learning agents, which learn directly from real execution results which candidate program will perform better, instead of predicting intermediate execution outcomes. The proposed model, ForeCritic, picks the better program 79.4% of the time on 12,438 held-out pairs from 26 ML tasks, compared with 53% to 62% for general-purpose LLM judges. When integrated into AIDE, ML-Master, and ForeAgent, it cuts mean task time by 4.4 to 7.5 times while keeping mean scores within 0.01 or raising them. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose world reward models that directly select the better candidate program without predicting execution outcomes, report proofs and 12,438 held-out pair evaluations, and test speedups w

entry.title: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
entry.summary: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies self-improving LLM agents that edit their own prompts and rules, keeping edits only when an acceptance gate scores them higher on task batches. Because overlapping safeguards mask the effect of deleting one, the gate can approve harmful changes based on task success alone, eroding redundancy unseen. The authors measured harm across all subsets of four safeguards in two environments, running 411 improvement loops under ten gate rules. They also report that evaluation batch size and the statistical test used affect which safeguards are kept. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show acceptance gates erode redundant safeguards via masking, reporting 411 controlled loops and a frozen predictive model.

entry.title: Reliable, scalable, value-aligned generative recommendation for large-scale advertising (GR4AD-X)
entry.summary: Towards Reliable, Scalable, and Value-Aligned Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents GR4AD-X, an advertising recommendation framework for the Kuaishou platform that generates discrete semantic identifiers autoregressively. It improves semantic identifier reliability with Multi-Path assignment, scales model capacity along several dimensions under serving constraints, and aligns generation with commercial value through the UniVGD method. Large-scale online A/B tests on Kuaishou's advertising platform show a 3.07% cumulative revenue gain over the deployed GR4AD baseline while meeting latency and throughput requirements. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose Multi-Path SID assignment, multi-dimensional capacity scaling, and unified value alignment, reporting a 3.07% revenue gain in large-scale Kuaishou online A/B tests.

entry.title: Optimal Regret Bounds for Communication-Efficient Decentralized Online Learning
entry.summary: Optimal Regret for Communication-Efficient Decentralized Online Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies decentralized online convex optimization where networked learners minimize a sequence of global losses using only local losses and compressed messages from neighbors. The authors propose Ascent-gossip, which combines an online compression strategy with a Chebyshev recursion to reach consensus faster than existing compressed gossip methods. Using this method, they present an online algorithm whose regret bounds for convex and strongly convex losses match known lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine online compression with Chebyshev recursion, reporting regret bounds matching lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Foundations for Undiscounted Bisimulation Metrics
entry.summary: Game-Theoretic Foundations for Undiscounted Bisimulation Metrics arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Bisimulation metrics measure task-relevant state similarity in reinforcement learning, but existing constructions mostly cover discounted MDPs. This paper reinterprets these metrics as game value functions of zero-sum turn-based games, giving unique definitions for total- and average-reward settings. It also analyzes how metric finiteness depends on MDP structure and shows that the metrics bound total-reward and optimal relative value differences. Error and suboptimality guarantees for aggregation-based planning are provided. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recast bisimulation metrics as zero-sum game values, giving unique definitions for undiscounted total- and average-reward MDPs, with bounds on value differences and aggregation-planning er

entry.title: ParaTTT: Parallelizing Test-Time Training Layers with Deep Memories
entry.summary: ParaTTT: Parallelizing Test-Time Training Layers with Deep Memories arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces ParaTTT (PTTT), an algorithm that parallelizes deep nonlinear memories in test-time training layers by iteratively refining estimates of the inner-loop gradient trajectory. Each refinement uses three chunkwise-parallel passes, and the exact online gradient descent recurrence is a fixed point of the iteration. With two refinement steps at 4K context, the inner-loop evaluation is reported to be 32 times faster than TTT-MLP with block approximation at matched error, and the 340M model trains 4.9 times faster. Models at 340M and 1.3B parameters match or exceed Gated DeltaNet and Mamba-2 on language-modeling perplexity and zero-shot accuracy, with better recall than linear recurrences. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose iterative chunkwise-parallel refinement for deep nonlinear test-time training memories, report 340M and 1.3B model comparisons, and give a convergence proof for a two-layer variant

entry.title: Near-optimal regret for adversarial linear bandits under strong corruption
entry.summary: Nearly Minimax Optimal Regret for Adversarial Linear Bandits with Strong Corruptions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies adversarial linear bandits where a strong adversary corrupts observed rewards after seeing the learner's action, within a known total corruption budget C. The authors propose CRW-FTRL, which uses a radius-weighted entropy regularizer and a normalized kernel estimator whose corruption sensitivity depends on per-action radii. The algorithm achieves regret that matches the best corruption-free rate and the corruption lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Applied to discretized general compact action sets, it yields regret of order d√T plus dC. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a radius-weighted regularizer achieving near-minimax regret under strong corruption, matching the corruption-free rate up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent AI
entry.summary: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines demographic bias when clinical large language models operate as multi-agent teams. Testing five model families and four aggregation topologies on 120 MIMIC-IV emergency cases with counterfactual demographic swaps, all configurations preserved the direction of individual agents' answers, giving Black patients more acute triage. The authors report that fairness instructions and demographic masking did not close the gap, while a diverse-perspective ensemble that pools counterfactual versions during deliberation reduced the disparity by 67 to 94%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce disparity laundering and report a full factorial of five model families and four topologies on 120 MIMIC-IV cases under counterfactual swaps.

entry.title: Annealed, Averaged Markov Chains Reach the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA (Part II: Langevin Dynamics)
entry.summary: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part II: Langevin Dynamics arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies tensor principal components analysis on the sphere, where an unknown vector must be recovered from a noisy observation of its k-th tensor power. The authors show that spherical Langevin dynamics, combined with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization. Together with Part I, the results show that local Markov chains can succeed down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show annealed, averaged spherical Langevin dynamics recovers tensor PCA signal in polynomial time above the algorithmic threshold from random initialization, continuing Part I.

entry.title: DecompGym: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Designing Decomposition Algorithms
entry.summary: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces DecompGym, a benchmark of 81 optimization instances from nine problem families, including five Benders and four column generation tasks, where agents must write solvers for prescribed decomposition methods. Each solver is checked for running within 60 seconds, numerical feasibility, an LLM judge's audit of the method used, and an objective within 1% of the stored optimum. Evaluating 12 GPT, Claude, and Gemini models over up to ten attempts, the authors find that reflection, which diagnoses failures first, succeeds on 66% of retries versus 39% for independent regeneration. The study concludes that decomposition agents need checks on how a solver reaches its answer, not only output checks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a 81-instance benchmark testing LLM agents on Benders and column generation, comparing regeneration with reflection across 12 models, and separating output checks from method audits.

entry.title: BridgeRouter: Per-instance routing among cross-modal bridge pathways for biosignal models
entry.summary: BridgeRouter: Gain-Aware Instance Routing over Cross-Modal Bridge Portfolios arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses transferring pretrained EEG foundation models to other biosignals without retraining their backbones. Instead of one global bridge pathway, BridgeRouter selects one of several frozen cross-modal pathways per instance, falling back to a validation-selected default route. It is evaluated on EMG-based freezing-of-gait detection and ECG-based sleep classification, where it improves balanced accuracy over the best single route.

entry.title: Theoretical Limits and Guarantees for Graph-Based Nearest-Neighbor Search
entry.summary: On Worst-Case Guarantees for Graph-Based Nearest-Neighbor Search arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the theoretical guarantees of graph-based nearest neighbor search methods such as HNSW, DiskANN, and NSG, which perform well in practice. The authors prove that standard graph-based methods running greedy search on flat or hierarchical graphs cannot achieve sublinear query time in Euclidean space, even with arbitrarily large approximation factors. They show that allowing Steiner points in the search graph makes sublinear query time possible, with bounds comparable to LSH, and include initial experiments on incorporating Steiner points into practical methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove standard graph-based search cannot achieve sublinear query time, and that Steiner points yield LSH-comparable bounds, with initial experiments.

entry.title: What LOL Measures: Hidden Label Shifts in Low-Light Enhancement Benchmarks
entry.summary: What Does LOL Measure? Hidden Label Shifts in Low-Light Enhancement Benchmarks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper audits the standard low-light image enhancement benchmarks LOL-v1 and LOLv2-Real using 18 public checkpoints from eight methods. It finds that test labels differ from training labels, with LOL-v1 test labels rendered differently and LOLv2-Real test labels darker than its training labels. The authors show that test-set checkpoint selection and released test-time settings affect reported scores and method rankings, and they provide reporting recommendations. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors audit 18 checkpoints of eight methods, report hidden label shifts in LOL benchmarks, and quantify their effect on rankings.

entry.title: Post-training LLMs with LLMON for safer instruction handling
entry.summary: Post-Training Large Language Models with LLMON arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a post-training method using LLMON (LLM Object Notation), which separates executable instructions from passive data and requires identifier-based execution. The authors built a 4.6B-token structured training corpus and post-trained Granite-4.1 3B and 8B base models with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. They report that attack success rates on indirect prompt-injection benchmarks fell from 53-100% to 0.02-5.6% while general capabilities were preserved. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that LLMON-structured post-training cuts indirect prompt-injection success rates substantially on two Granite models, and introduce attention-based interpretability metrics.

entry.title: Predicting Which Pages AI Answer Engines Cite, with Open Models and a 4B Student
entry.summary: Predicting What Answer Engines Cite: Open Decision Models, Rerankers and a Distilled 4B Student on Ten Engines under Controlled Retrieval arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to rank candidate web pages by how often answer engines will cite them in generated responses. The authors evaluate pretrained rerankers, a hosted decision model, eight open decision models, and distilled students on GEO-Bench queries across ten engines. A 4B student model fine-tuned from Qwen3-Reranker-4B performs comparably to the strongest scorers, and the model, benchmark, predictions, and code are released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report comparing rerankers and distilled 4B students against teacher decision models on GEO-Bench across ten answer engines.

entry.title: Vision Tomography: Portable 3D Face-Skull Reconstruction from Visual Data
entry.summary: Vision Tomography: Towards Portable 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Inference from Visual Data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Vision Tomography (VT), a framework that reconstructs paired 3D face and skull geometry from visual inputs such as images or sketches. The authors built a dataset of over 200 cases with CT skulls, CT faces, and textured face scans, and proposed a 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Morphable Model (BFSM) that infers shape between face and skull via a shared coefficient space. The framework is demonstrated in forensic and medical applications, including paired reconstruction and predicting surgical outcomes through joint face-skull editing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a bidirectional face-skull morphable model and a 200-plus sample dataset for paired 3D reconstruction from visual data, reporting experiments in forensic and medical applications.

entry.title: Integral Probability Boundaries: Tighter Non-Linear Bounds Than Integral Probability Metrics
entry.summary: Integral Probability Boundaries arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Integral Probability Boundaries (IPBs), a non-linear generalization of Integral Probability Metrics (IPMs). IPMs reduce the gap between two distributions to a single worst-case difference in expectations, which can yield loose or vacuous bounds for rare events, safety failures, or under-represented groups. IPBs are designed to remain tight at these extremes. The authors derive their basic properties, present estimation algorithms, and demonstrate use in alignment, judge-free performance estimation, and fairness, including more precise fairness-gap estimates for rare groups in a generative modeling task than prior methods.

entry.title: Who Else Is In? How AI Agents Might Start Secret Collusion Using Vague Messages
entry.summary: Who Else Is In? Multi-Agent Collusion Initation Via Strategic Vagueness arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how multi-agent LLM systems could begin collusion, with agents using vague public messages to find hidden partners while appearing to do ordinary work. The authors run a mutual identification game in which two agents must recognize each other while solving a shared task, and some models succeed without explicit guidance, often evading monitors at low false positive rates. They report that as messages grow more indirect, monitor punishment can fall faster than partner coordination, creating a profitable middle ground. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a mutual identification game showing strategic vagueness can initiate collusion past monitors; the abstract reports successful handshakes and an asymmetric monitor-punishment ver

entry.title: Human-Residual Steering: Aligning Frozen LLM Judges with Human Judgment Distributions
entry.summary: Human-Residual Steering: Aligning Frozen LLM Judges with Human Judgment Distributions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes Human-Residual Steering (HRS), a method that aligns frozen large language model judges with the distribution of individual human ratings by learning hidden-state interventions. Across 14 benchmarks and four judges from three model families, HRS outperforms all evaluated frozen-weight baselines on distribution matching. It also trains about 88 times fewer parameters than distributional fine-tuning. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose learned hidden-state interventions to align frozen LLM judges with human distributions, reporting gains across 14 benchmarks with far fewer trained parameters.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift
entry.summary: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies conformal prediction under covariate shift when the covariate density ratio is known, aiming for prediction sets with minimal expected length under the target distribution. For every calibration sample size, the authors prove that combining an inverse conditional-density score with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes expected length among all rules valid over the weighted-exchangeability class. They approximate the oracle with quantile and kernel histograms, including forest-weighted estimators, and select estimators and tuning parameters by resampling. Experiments on 36 known-density configurations and four public regression datasets compare coverage, set length, and runtime with existing methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the inverse-density score with randomized weighted calibration minimizes expected set length over weighted-exchangeable rules, and report experiments on 36 density configurations and

entry.title: Lower bound for projection-free online learning with linear oracles
entry.summary: An Ω(T³/4) lower bound for projection-free online learning with linear minimization oracles arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies projection-free online learning algorithms that handle the decision set using linear minimization oracles. Prior work showed that Online Frank-Wolfe achieves regret scaling as T^{3/4} under specific tunings, but whether all tunings do so was open. The authors prove a universal worst-case regret lower bound of Ω(T^{3/4} m^{-1/4}) for any projection-free algorithm making at most m oracle calls per round. They also propose an extended Online Frank-Wolfe that uses multiple linear optimizations per round and prove a regret upper bound of O(max{T^{3/4} m^{-1/4}, √T}). ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a universal regret lower bound for projection-free algorithms and match it with an extended OFW upper bound, answering an open question.

entry.title: Early Signs of Feature Learning in Deep Linear Networks
entry.summary: Investigating the Early Signatures of Feature Learning in Deep Linear Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper analyzes features learned by a deep linear network in a mean-field parameterization after a single gradient step from initialization, using high-dimensional data with a low-dimensional spiked signal. It derives closed-form expressions for the bias, variance, and generalization error of kernel ridge regression on these features. A one-step generalization advantage appears only when spike strength and effective signal-to-noise ratio are sufficiently large, and it vanishes for isotropic inputs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a closed-form account of one-step feature learning in mean-field deep linear networks and derive bias, variance, and generalization error expressions.

entry.title: Choosing Random Mixtures of AI Versions with Fewest Stakeholder Rejections
entry.summary: Learning Lotteries with Minimal Stakeholder Violations from Membership Queries arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies how to pick a randomized mixture of several candidate AI system versions that the fewest stakeholders reject. Each stakeholder accepts only mixtures inside an unknown halfspace, and the developer can learn this only by asking yes-or-no membership queries. The authors show that minimizing rejections is APX-hard in general, give exact algorithms for special cases, and provide approximation guarantees when only some stakeholders can be queried. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model stakeholder acceptance as unknown halfspaces, prove APX-hardness for minimizing rejections, and give polynomial and quasi-polynomial exact algorithms with sampling guarantees, plus s

entry.title: TACOS: Terrain-aware contact supervision method for visual footstep planning
entry.summary: TACOS: Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision for Visual Footstep Planning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents TACOS, a method that builds a footstep instability score from the residual of a factor graph used in legged robot state estimation, then projects that score onto earlier camera images to train a dense visual predictor. It proposes a hard score that uses hindsight and a causal soft score available immediately. On 1716 manually annotated contacts and three outdoor test runs, both variants outperform the compared alternatives at detecting instability and ranking its severity. In a real-world 50 m forest trial, the trained predictor handles mud and vegetation and steps around fallen branches. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a footstep instability score from factor-graph residuals to supervise a visual predictor, compared against baselines on 1716 annotated contacts and outdoor runs.

entry.title: WebAnything: Automatically Building Reusable Web Environments from Real Sites for AI Agents
entry.summary: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments arXiv · Oct 28, 2026WebAnything is a framework that automatically rebuilds reusable, resettable website environments from real URLs, so web agents can be trained and tested without manual per-site setup. It constructed 244 website environments across 14 application domains, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. In a blind audit it outperformed the human-assisted WebHarbor on three fidelity metrics. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction trajectories improved success rates on several benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors automate reconstruction of reusable web environments from real URLs with an independent verifier, reporting 244 sites and gains from fine-tuning on 5,856 trajectories.

entry.title: How much a weight update changes a model, compared across training stages
entry.summary: What a Weight Update Buys: Leverage Across Training Stages arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces leverage, a measure of how much a unit of weight change affects a language model's behavior, and applies it to released Olmo-3, Tülu-3, Zephyr, and OLMo-2 checkpoints. It finds that pretraining updates act like random directions on prose, while SFT, RL, and DPO stages show much higher leverage, up to about 23,000 for DPO. The authors also study how training precision and DARE random drop-and-rescale affect these measurements. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce leverage, a Fisher-form measure of weight update effect, comparing training stages across released checkpoints and deriving a DARE reuse law.

entry.title: Noise-robust Adam variant that trusts stable gradient signs
entry.summary: Moment-Guided Optimizers for Noisy Deep Learning: MGO-SC as a Simple Consistency Gate for Adam-Style Updates arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes MGO-SC, a lightweight modification of Adam-style optimizers that gates each coordinate's update by the stability of its gradient sign. A mean-preserving variant reallocates trust across coordinates without changing the net per-tensor step size. On CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18, it improves over an AdamW baseline under clean and noisy labels, with bootstrap confidence intervals and Wilcoxon tests reported.

entry.title: Relevance-guided residual calibration for compressing dense retrieval embeddings
entry.summary: Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration for Spectral Compression of Dense Retrieval Embeddings arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses spectral compression of dense retrieval embeddings, noting that existing corpus-derived weighting rules do not account for each retained direction's contribution to relevance. The authors propose Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration (RRC), a closed-form method that uses relevance judgments to refine spectral weights while preserving the compressor's overall trend. Experiments on nine datasets report that SpecTemp combined with RRC achieves the highest mean effectiveness among tested compressors on BEIR and BRIGHT, and the gains persist under scalar and product quantization. ★★★★ Notable: The authors add relevance-guided per-direction residual calibration to spectral compression, reporting gains over SpecTemp on nine BEIR and BRIGHT datasets.

entry.title: Network Structure Doesn't Matter: Classical Consensus Theory Fails for LLM Groups
entry.summary: Network Topology Does Not Matter: The Breakdown of Classical Consensus in LLM Populations arXiv · Oct 25, 2026This paper studies how networks of multiple large language models reach collective agreement. Using eight instruction-tuned models and 73,080 controlled exchanges, the authors measure the models' update behavior and find that they often update outside the range of observed opinions and show active repulsion through negative weights. In simulations of 10,000 agents, network connectivity explains almost none of the outcome variance, while the models' internal update bias and message framing largely govern population dynamics. The authors conclude that classical graph-theoretic metrics are inadequate for LLM populations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors challenge classical consensus assumptions, measure LLM update operators empirically, and report simulations of 10,000 agents.

entry.title: Measuring Hallucinations: Semantic Illusion, Confabulation, and Expressed Uncertainty
entry.summary: What Hallucinations Have We Measured? Semantic Illusion, Confabulation, and Expressed Uncertainty arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper argues for a strict definition of hallucinations in large language models as confident incorrectness, separate from expressed uncertainty. It proposes a re-elicitation test that splits errors into semantic illusions, where correct knowledge is accessible, and confabulations, where it is not. Re-evaluating 14 recent hallucination methods, the authors find that detectors flag expressed uncertainty more often than hallucinations, and that mitigation works far better for semantic illusions than for confabulations.

entry.title: Self-Consistency Geometry Injection for Multi-view Consistent Image Generation: a method that judges how reliable predicted geometry is by checking agreement across repeated predictions, then scales geometric guidance accordingly to improve multi-view image quality.
entry.summary: Self-Consistency Geometry Injection for Multi-view Consistent Image Generation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes RGMV, a reliability-guided multi-view generation method with a parameter-free Self-Consistency Geometry Gate (SCG) and a Reliability-aware Geometry Injection (RGI) module. It generates several geometry predictions for the same reference image and target viewpoints, measures their spatial agreement to form a reliability map, and uses this map to modulate how strongly geometry-conditioned residuals are injected into RGB synthesis. According to the authors, experiments show that this reliability-aware injection improves the geometric quality of multi-view generation.

entry.title: AtomSteer: Test-Time Constraint Steering for Atomistic Generative Models
entry.summary: AtomSteer: Test-Time Constraint Steering for Atomistic Generative Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes AtomSteer, a framework that steers pretrained atomistic generative models at inference time so their outputs satisfy structural constraints such as crystallographic symmetry, geometry, and stereochemistry. During sampling, it corrects intermediate structures using bounded local projections, graph-rigid stereochemical transformations, and projections over periodic symmetries, while limiting changes elsewhere. The method is tested on FlowMM, ET-Flow, and Boltz-2 across crystal generation, molecular conformer generation, and protein-ligand complex prediction, without retraining or architectural changes.

entry.title: Breaking Symmetry to Leave the Cave: Identifiable Structure Aids Cross-Lingual Generalization
entry.summary: Leaving the Cave by Breaking the Symmetry: Identifiable Structure Can Enable Cross-Lingual Generalization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper asks why multilingual models generalize across languages without a shared vocabulary and proposes the Relational Identifiability Hypothesis, which holds that relations in a shared world can rule out alternative cross-lingual correspondences and make corresponding entities more directly readable. The authors test this in a controlled bilingual Transformer trained on two token-disjoint languages describing the same modular-arithmetic world. Cross-lingual alignment emerges selectively when relations constrain number correspondences, and these patterns predict success in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer.

entry.title: SaiVLA-JEPA: Testing Whether Predicting Future Latent Features Improves Robot Control
entry.summary: SaiVLA-JEPA: Evaluating Future Latent Prediction in JEPA-Conditioned VLA Control arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies whether a vision-language-action robot policy that uses V-JEPA visual features benefits from a predictive training objective. The authors build SaiVLA-JEPA, which pairs a vision-language model with a diffusion transformer action expert, and compare variants on 10,030 paired LIBERO-Plus episodes. Adding current JEPA conditioning raised success to about 82.5% from 71.6% without JEPA, while extra future supervision gave no detectable overall gain at the tested training budget.

entry.title: UnMixMamba: Unmixing-Guided State-Space Subpixel Crop Mapping from MODIS Time Series
entry.summary: UnMixMamba: Unmixing Guided State Space Subpixel Mapping of Crops from MODIS Time Series arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes UnMixMamba, a method for mapping crop types from 250 m MODIS time series to field-scale AAFC labels. It estimates simplex fractions through a temporal-spectral-spatial decoupled factorization and reconstructs the MODIS data using abundance super-resolution and a learnable per-crop endmember bank. The predicted crop fractions direct high-resolution refinement toward the minority class. On Alberta 2015 under a fixed spatial-block protocol, it outperforms several baselines on overall accuracy, mIoU, and Kappa.

entry.title: Residual motion splatting for continuous space-time video super-resolution
entry.summary: Residual Motion Splatting for Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses continuous space-time video super-resolution, which turns a low-resolution, low-frame-rate video into a high-resolution, high-frame-rate one at arbitrary scales and times. The method predicts per-pixel continuous trajectories that refine optical-flow paths with smooth residual motion, then splats consecutive low-resolution latent features onto a high-resolution grid at predicted sub-pixel positions and visibility weights. A decoder resolves remaining ambiguities, making temporal interpolation and multi-frame super-resolution one operation. The authors report better fidelity and perceptual quality on several benchmarks, with speeds up to an order of magnitude faster.

entry.title: Camera-based vehicle density estimation for adaptive traffic signal control
entry.summary: Vision-Based Density Estimation for Adaptive Traffic Control arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a framework that optimizes traffic flow directly from camera images, with three parts: vehicle density estimation, predictive dynamics modeling, and signal policy optimization. The density estimation stage was evaluated on 40 annotated intersection images from Rambagh 4, Jaipur, India, reporting a five-fold validation mean absolute error of 3.32 ± 0.95 vehicles and a mean absolute percentage error of 14.5%. Empirical training and evaluation of the forecasting and control stages are left for future work.

entry.title: Faster nonlinear MPC via behavior cloning with separated timescales, applied to nuclear reactor load-following
entry.summary: Accelerating Nonlinear MPC by Behavior Cloning with Separated Timescales: Application to Nuclear Reactor Load-Following arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes SRLBC, a behavior cloning architecture that uses separate embeddings for slow state variables, fast stiff state variables, and exogenous inputs in multiscale systems. On 500 long-horizon roll-outs of a pressurized water reactor load-following benchmark, separated embeddings outperform shared-embedding baselines on cost, imitation accuracy, and constraint satisfaction. Embedded in a safety-augmented approximate NMPC framework, the controllers are about 6.8 times faster than NMPC with feasibility of at least 99.8%.

entry.title: Test-time calibration of track-query updates for multi-object tracking
entry.summary: Calibrating Track-Query Updates at Test Time for Multi-Object Tracking arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies identity switches in query-propagation multi-object trackers, which often occur when visually similar targets overlap or cross. The authors find that propagated track queries change more abruptly before switches, and that current-frame updates point more strongly toward nearby active tracks. They propose Test-time Track-Query Calibration (TQC), a training-free, gradient-free method that applies a bounded correction before propagation. On nine DanceTrack and SportsMOT test settings, TQC improves HOTA and AssA in all settings, with an average HOTA gain of +0.38.

entry.title: Beyond Reachability: When Edit Order Preserves Couplings in Graph Flow Matching
entry.summary: Beyond Reachability: When Edit Order Preserves Couplings in Graph Flow Matching arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies whether reordering legal shortest edits in a graph generator can preserve a prescribed source-target pairing without changing the pairing, mandatory edits, or sampling budget. Under a common Poisson clock, it gives an exact criterion: the memoryless Markov projection reaches the unavoidable clock-error floor if and only if routes to distinct targets share no graph states. The work also proposes a legality-preserving scheduling procedure with recovery certificates.

entry.title: Geometry-aware trajectory state modeling for few-shot action recognition
entry.summary: Geometry-Aware Trajectory State Modeling for Few-Shot Action Recognition arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes GeoTRAM, a framework for few-shot action recognition that lifts sparse point tracks into 2.5D trajectories. It uses StateMotion to model ordered state evolution within each trajectory and RelMotion to capture local interactions through time-varying relative geometry and motion. The method adds quality-filtered spectral sampling, separately refined semantic, motion, and depth cues, and action-guided reweighting with top-ρ trajectory selection. Experiments on five benchmarks show strong gains on the motion-centric Something-Something datasets and competitive results on appearance-driven ones.

entry.title: CineU: Agentic System for Language-Driven Scene and Camera Control in Unreal Engine
entry.summary: Cinematize from Unreal: Agentic Choreography for Controllable World Simulation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper presents CineU (Cinematize from Unreal), an agentic system that uses language to orchestrate worlds and cinematic choreography inside Unreal Engine. It treats the Unreal project as a persistent, inspectable world representation, with agent-generated code whose effects are executed and verified. The system combines hierarchical orchestration, asset retrieval with geometry-constrained placement, code synthesis, and multi-stage verification with localized repair. Experiments on scene construction, selective editing, and multi-shot cinematography show that engine feedback improves task completion and recovery.

entry.title: Automatic Iconographic Annotation of Medieval Illuminations: Comparing Generative and Discriminative Models
entry.summary: Automatic Iconographic Annotation of Medieval Illuminations: Comparing Generative Vision-Language Models and Supervised Discriminative Classifiers arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper compares two approaches for automatically tagging the iconography of medieval manuscript illuminations, using 9,735 full-folio images labelled with 2,333 TIMEL concepts. It tests generative vision-language models against supervised discriminative classifiers, with ML-Decoder achieving the strongest retrieval results (precision@1 of 0.696, MRR of 0.806). The authors conclude the two paradigms are complementary and propose a soft F1 metric that credits taxonomically close predictions.

entry.title: When Support Crosses the Line: Evaluating Ethical Boundaries of LLM Mental Health Support in China
entry.summary: When Support Crosses the Line: Evaluating Ethical Boundaries in LLM-Based Mental Health Support in the Chinese Context arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces MindEth-Bench, a benchmark that tests whether large language models keep to professional ethical boundaries in multi-turn mental health conversations. It is grounded in Chinese professional ethical standards for mental health services and uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to generate interaction paths that stress-test model boundaries. Experiments on nine LLMs show that models responding appropriately at first can drift into ethical violations over longer exchanges, with wide variation across models and dimensions. The authors conclude that single-turn evaluations may overestimate the ethical reliability of such systems.

entry.title: CoSTA: Co-Evolving Self-Play Agents for Complex Temporal Knowledge Graph QA
entry.summary: CoSTA: Co-Evolving Self-Play Timeline Agents for Complex Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses complex temporal knowledge graph question answering, where the time constraints of one fact affect the search for others. It proposes CoSTA, which organizes facts into navigable timelines, assigns investigations to worker agents, and has a coordinator synthesize their timestamped observations. A shared policy is initialized by role-conditioned distillation and then both roles are optimized jointly through co-evolving self-play with final-answer rewards. The authors report state-of-the-art overall performance on three benchmarks, with compact variants outperforming evaluated closed-source LLM agents.

entry.title: Comparing decision models and generative LLMs on medical multiple-choice questions
entry.summary: Benchmarking decision models against generative large language models on medical multiple-choice questions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper benchmarks 13 decision models against 15 generative large language model configurations on 1,273 four-option MedQA questions under text-only conditions. Accuracy ranged from 67.71% to 89.08% for decision models and 78.32% to 96.86% for generative configurations. Decision models showed resource advantages but lower peak accuracy. The authors argue model selection should weigh probability quality and repeatability along with accuracy and error-correction costs.

entry.title: DES-JEPA: Learning a Shared Vocabulary for High-Dimensional Discrete Event Sequences
entry.summary: DES-JEPA: Learning a Shared Vocabulary for High-Dimensional Discrete Event Sequences arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses discrete event sequences such as operational logs and patient clinical-event trajectories, whose event labels differ across domains and can number in the hundreds. It proposes DES-JEPA, which learns a shared discrete vocabulary from synthetic stochastic processes with unaligned event vocabularies, and DES-PFN, which uses that vocabulary for in-context next-event prediction. Without task-specific fine-tuning, the framework achieves competitive zero-shot performance on eight unseen real-world datasets and scales to 700 distinct event types.

entry.title: RoleFUZZER: Fuzzing User Behaviour to Test LLM Role-Specification Adherence
entry.summary: RoleFUZZER: User-Behaviour Fuzzing for Role-Specification Adherence in Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Large language models are often given roles such as tutor or financial advisor through system prompts, but how reliably they keep to these roles during multi-turn conversations with difficult users has been little studied. The paper proposes user behaviour fuzzing and introduces RoleFUZZER, a framework adapting coverage-guided fuzzing from software testing to search for user behaviours that cause role violations. Across five role specifications, the framework covers at least 89% of a 64-cell behaviour grid for every model and role tested, and reveals specification-grounded failure patterns. Compared with free-form user generation at the same budget, the grid-guided approach achieves higher coverage and finds more kinds of violations.

entry.title: Storage capacity of Hopfield-Hebbian dynamics when stored patterns are correlated
entry.summary: Capacity of the Hopfield-Hebbian dynamics with correlated patterns arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how many patterns a Hopfield-Hebbian associative memory network can reliably store when the patterns are correlated rather than independent. Each archetype pattern is replaced by M correlated examples, with a parameter r controlling the correlation quality. The authors use a Random Duality Theory framework to derive capacity characterizations that closely match simulated dynamics and explicitly show the effects of M and r.

entry.title: Continual Adaptation Across Modalities: How Unified Multimodal Models Learn and Forget
entry.summary: Continual Adaptation Across Modalities: Learning and Forgetting in Unified Multimodal Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how unified multimodal models, which handle several modalities in one framework, learn and forget when trained continually on tasks across modalities. It examines how architectural design and adaptation methods affect interference between the generation and understanding sides. The authors find that interference shrinks as modality-specific parameters are more isolated, that the generation side is more fragile than the understanding side, and that post-training abilities such as personalized generation drop by 84% to 90% while pretraining abilities stay stable.

entry.title: Whether models rely on their chain of thought more as they scale, regardless of post-training
entry.summary: Does Chain-of-Thought Reliance Follow a Scaling Law?Larger Models Follow Their Steps More, Independent of Post-Training arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The study tests how much a model's final answer depends on its own written reasoning steps, using a synthetic box-swap task where every intermediate state is known. The authors replace one step in the chain with a wrong but valid state and check whether the answer changes accordingly. Across 25 open-weight models, reliance rises with size and saturates, is driven mainly by capability, and is essentially unchanged by post-training.

entry.title: The Code Behind the Layout: AI Agents for Analog Layout Generators
entry.summary: The Code Behind the Layout: AI Agents for Analog Layout Generators arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Analog layout design remains largely manual and difficult to automate. The paper examines whether large language models should write or edit generator code for frameworks such as gLayout, comparing this with having models draw layouts directly in SKY130 through controlled experiments. The authors find that the main obstacle to direct layout drawing is time and token cost, while the main advantage of building on a generator framework is reusability.

entry.title: IntReal: A Real-World Benchmark for Text-Image Interleaved Generation by Multimodal Models
entry.summary: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces IntReal, which pairs IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of 100K multimodal interleaved samples across four categories, with an evaluation suite that measures models along seven complementary dimensions. The suite shows low redundancy between metrics and high agreement with human judgments. Benchmarking four families of unified multimodal models reveals distinct strengths and weaknesses, and post-training experiments show the dataset improves interleaved generation, while unimodal generation training also helps.

entry.title: Deeper Backpropagation or More Updates? Looped Language Model Training Across Budgets
entry.summary: Deeper Backpropagation or More Updates? Training Looped Language Models Across Budgets arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies how to choose the backward window in training looped language models, which sets how many final layer repetitions keep gradients. It compares window sizes across different training budgets, using training recipes of roughly equal time. The results show that shorter windows lose much of their advantage as budgets grow, so the preferred window depends on the budget.

entry.title: Weather image synthesis using structure-retaining low-rank adapters
entry.summary: Structure-retained low-rank adapters for weather synthesis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a weather synthesis method that uses structure-retaining Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA) on Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) to generate images under different weather conditions. The authors analyze which attention blocks in SDXL mainly process structural information during image-to-image translation, then learn structural LoRA matrices for those blocks, removing the need for external conditioning such as ControlNet. Experiments reportedly show greater realism than existing synthesis approaches while preserving scene structure. The authors suggest the pipeline can generate training and evaluation data for outdoor computer vision.

entry.title: Governance-aware federated learning for trustworthy multi-agent AI collaboration
entry.summary: Governance-Aware Federated Learning for Multi-Agent AI Systems: A Policy-Driven Framework for Trustworthy Collaborative AI arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes Governance-Aware Federated Learning (GAFL), which adds independent verification of governance evidence, trust tracking, fairness and explainability checks, anomaly detection, policy enforcement, and tamper-evident audit logging to federated learning. A 10-participant cross-silo prototype was tested on the Adult Income dataset under several honest, biased, malicious, and falsified-evidence scenarios. Complete GAFL identified all falsified-evidence participants, while the version without independent verification identified none, at a higher per-round governance processing cost than FedAvg.

entry.title: Keeping Diversity Across the Whole Search in LLM-Guided Evolution
entry.summary: Holistic Diversity Management in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes HoliDivEvolve, which maintains and uses diversity among evolving program islands throughout LLM-guided evolutionary search. It introduces diverse initialization, trajectory adaptive island selection based on current score, recent growth, and remaining budget, and growth adaptive migration to share ideas across islands. Experiments across diverse benchmarks show competitive performance on most evaluated tasks, and controlled analyses examine how design choices affect search behavior and final results.

entry.title: SpaceAct: A Benchmark for 3D Spatiotemporal Reasoning Through Closed-Loop Action and Active Perception
entry.summary: SpaceAct: Benchmarking 3D Spatial and Temporal Reasoning via Closed-Loop Action and Active Perception arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces SpaceAct, an interactive benchmark that tests multimodal large language models on 3D spatiotemporal reasoning through closed-loop physical action and active perception. It contains 108 verified instances across 36 task families, built on interlocking bricks and mechanical puzzles, and is paired with the SAPA agent framework. Models must rotate the camera to resolve occlusion, output 6-DoF poses, and pass collision and statics checks. Results show that even with a valid plan, models remain limited by 3D visual grounding and action refinement, while exact 3D state information sharply reduces collisions.

entry.title: LLMs as Judges and Examinees for Predicting Medical Exam Item Difficulty
entry.summary: LLMs as Judges and Examinees for Medical Item Difficulty Prediction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to predict the difficulty of medical exam questions from their text alone. Using USMLE and PANCE licensure exam items, open-weight large language models act as judges, giving absolute difficulty ratings and pairwise comparisons, and as simulated examinees, producing signals such as correctness and answer probabilities. Combining these signals with baseline item features yields Spearman correlations of 0.447 on USMLE and 0.494 on PANCE. These results are comparable to direct ratings from the proprietary model Claude Opus 5.

entry.title: Agent Transfer Protocol: a server-mediated way for agents across organizations to communicate
entry.summary: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Agent-to-Agent Communication Architecture for the Agentic Web arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes ATP (Agent Transfer Protocol), a cross-organization agent communication protocol that uses domain-mediated architecture. Administrative domains hold stable addresses and receiving entries for logical agents, and the domain servers of both parties handle cross-domain transmission. The receiving domain verifies and stores messages for later reading, while the sending domain signs the complete message envelope. The authors built a prototype and evaluated it with a controlled cross-organization LLM agent workflow, mechanism checks, and latency measurements.

entry.title: SCOPE: Selective Critical-Step Self-Distillation for Training AI Agents
entry.summary: SCOPE: Selective Critical-Step On-Policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes SCOPE, a training framework for long-horizon LLM agents that addresses the coarse supervision of outcome-based reinforcement learning. After a supervised warm-up, the policy reviews its own trajectories, generates step-specific hindsight skills, and distills guidance only at selected error steps, with a bounded signed coefficient and a success-relative pairwise length reward. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop report consistent gains across backbones, with Qwen2.5-3B reaching 97.7% and 85.2% success and Qwen3-32B reaching 94.0% on unseen ALFWorld tasks.

entry.title: Visually irrelevant hallucinations in medical AI models that describe images
entry.summary: Visually Irrelevant Hallucinations in Medical Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies hallucinations in medical vision-language models, where generated clinical statements lack visual support or contradict the image. The authors propose CLEAR, a model-agnostic post-hoc framework that estimates phrase-level hallucination risk using localized counterfactual image perturbations. CLEAR outperforms existing hallucination detection baselines on four datasets, raising AUPRC on MIMIC-CXR from 85.10% to 90.23%.

entry.title: Temporal link prediction using structural proximity
entry.summary: Revisiting Temporal Link Prediction through Structural Proximity arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper revisits temporal link prediction and shows that Personalized PageRank on historical interaction graphs, with sliding-window retention or exponential time decay, can match or outperform existing methods without training. Across 14 datasets, Time-decay PPR ranked first on nine and second on four. The authors argue that strong results do not necessarily require complex temporal models and call for reassessing progress with classical baselines.

entry.title: Pronunciation-supervised speech synthesis for Irish using dictionary-derived verification
entry.summary: Pronunciation-Supervised Text-to-Speech for Irish (Gaeilge) arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper adapts the pretrained Qwen3-TTS text-to-speech model to Irish using 12.8 hours of crowdsourced Common Voice speech. Its character error rate is 0.225 on held-out cross-corpus text, beating a from-scratch system (0.397) and zero-shot cloning (0.437). The authors convert Wiktionary pronunciation records into a phoneme critic and use it in one round of rejection fine-tuning, reducing cross-corpus error to 0.159. The study also finds that the training data is too skewed toward Munster to steer the voice toward the Ulster dialect.

entry.title: How much do teacher-written bridge segments matter in interleaved on-policy distillation?
entry.summary: How Much Do Teacher Bridges Matter in Interleaved On-Policy Distillation? arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies on-policy distillation, where a student model learns from teacher predictions on its own responses, and some methods insert teacher-written bridge segments into those responses. The authors compare no loss, forward KL, and reverse KL on identical trajectories, using Qwen3-1.7B as the student and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the teacher. In the main comparison, the three loss treatments were statistically equivalent in accuracy within a ±5 percentage-point margin, and no added benefit from teacher text was detected.

entry.title: SelfMorph: Letting Frozen LLMs Reshape Their Internal Computation Per Input
entry.summary: Compute Has Shape: Self-Morphing the Internal Computation of Frozen LLMs arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes SelfMorph, which chooses the internal computational structure of a large language model at inference time for each input. It combines the original forward path, serial reuse of a layer span, and local branching and merging of perturbed hidden states. A lightweight selector reads the hidden-state trajectory on the prompt to pick a morphology, trained by distilling a utility distribution from offline morphing. Across three models from 4B to 27B, it reports mean relative gains of 8.06% on in-distribution benchmarks and 4.45% on unseen benchmarks.

entry.title: TCC-RAG: Temporal Causal Chain-Guided Retrieval for Answering Questions over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
entry.summary: TCC-RAG: Temporal Causal Chain-Guided RAG for Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses a limitation of semantic retrieval-augmented generation for temporal knowledge graph question answering, namely its difficulty capturing multi-hop causal knowledge and its tendency to add redundant information. The authors propose TCC-RAG, which converts the temporal knowledge graph into a multi-view causal cue graph, builds a query-specific temporal causal chain to guide retrieval, and uses a causal evidence filter to refine the results. Experiments report gains of 10.72% and 8.40% on two TKGQA benchmarks and a 62.97% improvement for multi-step temporal reasoning.

entry.title: SparseTokenGS: a Gaussian-based method for reconstructing 3D CT images from few X-ray views
entry.summary: SparseTokenGS: Gaussian-based Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction via Reusable Token Pool arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes SparseTokenGS, a method for reconstructing cone-beam CT volumes from sparse projection views, which otherwise produce severe artifacts. It uses a reusable token pool so that scan-wide context remains available during coordinate decoding, and reconstructs the volume in a single forward pass. On three public chest and dental datasets it achieves the highest reconstruction performance among the compared methods.

entry.title: Volley3D: Reconstructing Full Volleyball Sequences in 3D from Single-Camera Broadcasts
entry.summary: Volley3D: Unified 3D Full-Sequence Reconstruction from Monocular Broadcasts arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Volley3D is a pipeline for reconstructing volleyball play in 3D from monocular broadcast video, without using 3D training supervision. It corrects player positions using jump detection and Newtonian interpolation, and estimates ball trajectories through sub-trajectory segmentation and collision matching anchored to reconstructed 3D hand vertices. The authors report that on multi-camera benchmarks, the approach significantly reduces 3D spatial drift compared with 2D-reprojection baselines.

entry.title: CSO: Refining Robot Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Level Optimization
entry.summary: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes Cascaded Skills Optimization (CSO), a two-stage post-training framework for improving robotic manipulation policies built on discrete skills. The first stage uses rejection-sampling supervised fine-tuning to align the observation-to-skill mapping with the distribution of successful online trajectories. The second stage freezes the observation encoder and computes an independent, clipped importance ratio for each complete skill to enable stable updates. Using a lightweight QueST-style policy, CSO raises overall LIBERO success from 80.1% to 97.5% and reaches 61.0% success across five physical single-arm tasks.

entry.title: Encode Once, Answer Many: Method That Stores Document Context in Model Weights
entry.summary: Encode Once, Answer Many: Internalizing Context via Parametric Flow arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes CLIK, a generator that turns a given context into LoRA parameters in a single forward pass, which are then inserted into a frozen base model. The model can then answer queries from the question alone, without re-reading the context. On document question answering, CLIK clearly beats the no-context base model and prior hypernetwork generators, though it still trails a model that reads the context directly. It also transfers to multi-turn dialogue without multi-turn-specific training.

entry.title: WeVisCut: A single agent for editing long videos from narration
entry.summary: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video arXiv · Oct 28, 2026WeVisCut is a system that turns narration scripts into long-form videos by linking tool execution with policy learning in one agent harness. The authors build a four-stage data pipeline that recovers editing intent from finished videos and replays it as executable training data, yielding over 130K examples. They train a single 9B policy on this data that coordinates production and recovers from failures, and introduce a 100-task benchmark with five metrics.

entry.title: Aligning Misaligned Benchmarks for Single-View Novel View Synthesis
entry.summary: Aligning Misaligned Benchmarks for Single-View Novel View Synthesis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper shows that evaluating single-view novel view synthesis depends heavily on how each method's reference frame is aligned with the ground-truth pose. The authors align 3D reconstructions using traditional 2D-to-2D and 2D-to-3D image matching and evaluate only within co-visible regions. With proper alignment, explicit 3D Gaussian methods reach state-of-the-art performance. The paper also presents a simple baseline combining an off-the-shelf video generator and a feed-forward geometry estimator, which performs comparably to methods trained specifically for this task.

entry.title: Knowledge-structured, evidence-aware self-distillation for a glomerular pathology foundation model
entry.summary: Knowledge-structured and evidence-aware semantic self-distillation for glomerular pathology foundation model arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces GloSAGE, a self-distillation framework that uses lesion profiles predicted by a pretrained visual teacher to build structured pathology descriptions for glomerular images. It trains projection layers for image-text alignment while keeping the visual encoder frozen, and was developed on GloMillion. Evaluated across seven glomerulus- and case-level cohorts, it supports zero-shot lesion recognition and image-text retrieval. The authors suggest teacher-derived lesion profiles can provide annotation-efficient semantic supervision for a glomerular visual foundation model.

entry.title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI agents make stock investment decisions without seeing the future?
entry.summary: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future? arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces Investor's Last Exam (ILE), an equity-research benchmark designed with experienced buy-side investors and fund managers. It combines a versioned financial database with validated timestamps, a task taxonomy built around professional analyst deliverables, and a framework linking scoring criteria to sources, calculations, and assumptions. Across 86 assignments, it jointly assesses research quality, forecast accuracy, and simulated investment performance. Even the top models fail to convert overall research ability into predictive performance, with GPT-6 Astra scoring only 52.5 on Forecast & Model.

entry.title: Retrieving Statutes from Arabic Court Narratives: Saudi Family and Evidence Law
entry.summary: Statutory Article Retrieval from Arabic Judicial Narratives: Family Law and Law of Evidence in Saudi Arabia arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines how long factual narratives in Arabic court cases can be matched to statute articles that state abstract legal rules. The authors build a benchmark of 200 synthetic Saudi cases and 381 articles from the Family Law and Law of Evidence, and compare several retrieval methods. They propose a Decompose-and-Refine pipeline that splits each case into disputed issues and generates multiple retrieval queries per issue, which substantially improves retrieval for Evidence Law articles.

entry.title: Training a graph prior-data fitted network on structural causal model priors for graph foundation models
entry.summary: Learning a Prior-Data Fitted Network for Graph Foundation Models via Structural Causal Model Priors arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes GSCM-PFN, a graph prior-data fitted network pre-trained on synthetic graphs generated from a structural causal model (SCM) prior that jointly models nodes and graph topology. The authors design a joint feature-edge-label SCM to generate diverse synthetic graphs and a feature-permutation-invariant dual-path graph network. Experiments on 23 real-world benchmarks report that GSCM-PFN outperforms conventional and PFN-based graph foundation models without using real graph data for pre-training.

entry.title: Fu-TCM: A Multimodal AI Model Learning Traditional Chinese Medicine Diagnostic Reasoning
entry.summary: Fu-TCM: a multimodal large language model that learns traditional Chinese medicine diagnostic reasoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents Fu-TCM, a multimodal large language model for traditional Chinese medicine, trained on about 7.12 million examples drawn from classical texts, textbooks, medical images, clinical cases, and public datasets after cleaning and filtering. The model is further optimized with Bianzheng-Grounded Policy Optimization, which rewards response format, intermediate TCM reasoning fields, and final syndrome predictions. Fu-TCM-27B leads all six benchmarks covering TCM reasoning, text, and vision, reaching a macro-average accuracy of 81.01%.

entry.title: MUSE: Multi-level memory and selective injection for science coding agents
entry.summary: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces MUSE, a memory framework that helps scientific coding agents reuse past experience. It builds global, approach-level, and implementation-level memory from historical trajectories, injecting global and problem-matched approach memory at startup and selectively retrieving implementation memory during execution via an LLM gate. Across four benchmarks covering numerical problem solving, kernel optimization, and scientific software repair, MUSE outperforms retrieval and memory baselines on all metrics.

entry.title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right: A Soft Variant of MTP Training
entry.summary: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Multi-token prediction (MTP) is a common language-model pre-training method that improves downstream performance and speeds up inference through speculative decoding. The paper finds that a residual term in the standard MTP gradient interferes with learning, and the problem grows with scale. It proposes Soft-MTP, a one-line change that keeps only the KL self-distillation signal and removes the noisy residual, improving over standard MTP from 167M to 1.2B parameters without adding parameters.

entry.title: A case study of an AI agent loop that learns to optimize kernels for a new accelerator
entry.summary: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents an LLM agent loop built to write optimized kernels for AI accelerators whose architecture and language are rarely seen by language models. Using the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU as the example, the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days. It builds its own hardware knowledge from documentation summaries, microbenchmarks, and compiler-derived rules, and searches per-kernel design trees. The final kernels reach a 9.293x geomean speedup over the official baseline, each within 1.25x of the cycles needed to move its weights.

entry.title: Can LLMs Solve Ontology Tasks Faithfully? An Interpretability Study
entry.summary: Can LLMs Faithfully Solve Ontology Engineering Tasks? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces MIOE, a causal-abstraction benchmark that tests whether internal representations in language models truly encode ontological knowledge. It evaluates interchange interventions on entity typing and subsumption prediction tasks, using SAE-, DBM-, and DAS-based methods on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B. Distributed subspace methods perform best, showing that ontological predictions are mechanistically accessible in LLMs, though the causal mechanism is not yet cleanly disentangled.

entry.title: SSQA: Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention for Layered Modeling in Perception Tasks
entry.summary: SSQA: Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention for Hierarchical Modeling in Perception Tasks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention (SSQA), which models image tokens hierarchically as a full quadtree. The authors provide a complexity analysis showing linear-time feature modeling and compare inference speed with Mamba 2 and Quadtree Attention. Benchmarked across several tasks, SSQA reportedly achieves results at least as good as other methods, and sometimes better, at a fraction of the computational cost.

entry.title: Reconstructing CT Scans from Extremely Few Projections Using Pose-Aware Diffusion
entry.summary: Extremely Sparse-View Computed Tomography from 2D Projections via Pose-Aware Diffusion Priors arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses extremely sparse-view computed tomography, where only a few projections can be acquired due to scan time, motion, or radiation limits. The method learns a pose-aware diffusion prior from one 2D projection per training sample and guides diffusion sampling with measured-view fidelity, shared-volume reprojection, and projection-physics consistency. On two public CT datasets with 1, 4, and 8 views, it achieves the best novel-view synthesis scores and best or competitive reconstruction quality against baselines that use dense-volume supervision.

entry.title: What a Navigator Should Remember: Spatiotemporal Memory for Zero-Shot Navigation
entry.summary: What Should a Navigator Remember? Spatiotemporal Memory for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Navigation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies what an 8B-scale robot navigation system should store and how to organize it, without navigation-specific training. The system uses three complementary memories: task progress, pose-anchored compressed observation history, and accumulated geometry. On R2R-CE val-unseen, the full system achieves the highest success rate among the evaluated Qwen3-based zero-shot baselines, and removing temporal memory raises average path length from 16.9 m to 39.1 m. Real-world tests on a Unitree Go2 also show higher success than a post-trained baseline in corridor and office settings.

entry.title: LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute
entry.summary: LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces LLM-PowerTrace, an open dataset recording how each GPU's power draw changes over time during large language model fine-tuning and inference, sampled every 100 ms across varying NVIDIA platforms with workload and system metadata. It includes controlled sweeps over factors such as batch size, sequence length, precision, parallelism, concurrency, GPU frequency, quantization, and request-arrival patterns. The authors define power-grid-facing metrics from the traces and propose an AI-compute power and energy scaling law for extrapolating beyond the measured settings.

entry.title: CHORD: Detecting LLM Hallucinations Across Different Models Using Relational Graphs
