entry.summary: CHORD: Cross-Model Hallucination Detection via Relational Graph Discrimination arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies cross-model hallucination detection, training detectors on source language models and applying them to unseen target models. Because hidden states from different models are semantically inconsistent, classical representation-based detectors transfer poorly. The authors propose CHORD, which represents hidden states as joint relational graphs over layers, tokens, and features, and uses relation-aware attention with meta-learning. Experiments report better cross-model generalization than representative detection methods.

entry.title: Detecting LLM-written text robustly using matched condition response probing
entry.summary: Robust LLM-Generated Text Detection through Matched Conditional-Response Probing arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces MCRP, a framework that uses a frozen large language model to measure how a candidate text responds when a semantically matched condition is added, removed, or replaced. A lightweight random-forest classifier is trained on these response features to detect LLM-generated text. Under rewriting, polishing, and expansion, it reports 93.97% F1 and 96.24% ROC-AUC, and it performs consistently across multilingual and multidomain evaluations.

entry.title: Does 3D Pose Improve Football Action Valuation? A Study of Pose and Learning Choices
entry.summary: Does 3D Pose Improve Action Valuation in Football? An Empirical Study of Pose Representations and Learning Objectives arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether adding 3D player pose to a SARSA-based multi-agent reinforcement learning model improves value estimates for observed football actions. Using UEFA Champions League 2022/23 event, tracking and 3D pose data, the authors compare six pose representations across five learning settings. Pose rarely improved return prediction, while training choices had larger effects; pose did improve prediction of the on-ball action 0.2 seconds ahead and pass success.

entry.title: Inner-Learning: Moving From Hand-Coded Beliefs to Declarative Knowledge in Trick-Taking Card Games
entry.summary: Inner-Learning: From Hand-Coded Beliefs to Declarative Knowledge in Trick-Taking Games arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a declarative approach to modeling belief states in trick-taking card games. The authors automatically extract the hand-coded inference rules of a state-of-the-art Skat player into a domain-specific language and verify them through round-trip code generation. They also add cardinality constraints, and self-play results show the declarative engine improves winning percentage and score over the original engine.

entry.title: Visual token pruning before the LLM using spectral structure and text relevance
entry.summary: Don't Ask the LLM: Visual Token Pruning with Spectral Structure and Semantic Relevance arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper addresses the high inference cost of large vision-language models, which process long sequences of visual tokens. It proposes ST-Pruner, a training-free method that selects visual tokens before the large language model, combining attention-independent spectral saliency with inverted patch-text similarity via parameter-free multiplicative fusion. The authors report retaining over 95% of full-token performance using at most 11.1% of visual tokens across diverse models, and a 3.2x end-to-end speedup on LLaVA-NeXT.

entry.title: Hidden Commitment: How Language Models Silently Choose a Side and Steering to Reveal It
entry.summary: Hidden Commitment: When Language Models Silently Pick a Side and How Steering Can Surface It arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether language models, when answering from two conflicting documents, silently favor one source without disclosing the disagreement. In Qwen 0.8B, the authors find a residual source-choice direction whose sign tracks the document used, and steering this direction changes the chosen source. A transfer experiment on Gemma 3 1B reproduces the readout and sparse-write pattern. Conflict disclosure appears weaker, later in the network, and only partially steerable, so the authors propose monitoring residual readouts for silent source commitment.

entry.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting
entry.summary: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces EPSBench, a benchmark for testing how well LLM agents forecast a company's quarterly earnings per share (EPS). It covers 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies, where agents read filings, earnings-call transcripts and news, and estimate income-statement drivers with cited evidence. Six models are compared; three show no detectable difference from analyst consensus in point forecast error, while three have higher error. Nominal 80% prediction intervals contain reported EPS in only 37% to 70% of runs that return an interval.

entry.title: Vendster: An Arena Testing How Forecast Quality Shapes LLM Agent Behavior in Buyer-Vendor Negotiations
entry.summary: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer-Vendor Negotiation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces Vendster, an evaluation arena that measures how a forecaster's bias and prediction-interval width affect the outcome of a discount negotiation between buyer and vendor LLM agents. In the M5-based reference instance, model-generated forecasts raised sales target attainment by up to 17 percentage points, yet standard metrics like relWQL and MASE did not significantly predict negotiation outcomes. Experiments with synthetic forecasts found that the direction of bias and agents' forecast reactivity were more strongly associated with outcomes than forecast accuracy.

entry.title: PulmoWorld: An Asynchronous Multimodal World Model for Pneumonia Progression
entry.summary: PulmoWorld: An Asynchronous Multimodal Medical World Model for Longitudinal Pneumonia Dynamics arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents PulmoWorld, a world model that tracks how pneumonia evolves over time by combining asynchronous state estimation, recursive simulation, and evidence-constrained planning. On the MASS pneumonia cohort, its recursive forecasts are competitive with task-trained sequence models, and trained on public MIMIC-IV-CXR data it improves prognostic discrimination over latest-value fusion. The authors also introduce Cap-MBRL, which in five simulated environments with known mechanisms reduces selection regret compared with directly executing a fallback action.

entry.title: ConvRoute-ViT: Convolutional Token Routing for Faster Vision Transformers
entry.summary: ConvRoute-ViT: Convolutional Token Routing for Efficient Vision Transformers arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Vision Transformers face rising computational cost because self-attention grows quadratically with the number of input tokens. This paper proposes ConvRoute-ViT, which keeps the most relevant patch tokens at selected layers based on class-token attention and compresses the rest into compact convolutional summary tokens. The approach shortens the sequence while retaining some context from less informative tokens. Experiments on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet show improved computational efficiency with classification accuracy maintained relative to the base ViT.

entry.title: Human Evaluation with Automatic Scores: Separating Sampling and Estimation Gains
entry.summary: Human Evaluation with Automatic Scores: Separating Sampling and Estimation Gains arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines how automatic judge scores can reduce the number of human annotations needed for model evaluation. It compares three uses of the scores (guiding sampling, correcting estimates, and supporting adaptive acquisition) on fixed pools from three preference datasets and 19 attributed question-answering systems. After ten-bin score stratification, the best local linear correction reduces mean squared error by only 1.00 to 5.27% further. The authors recommend proportional sampling within score strata followed by a stratified human mean as a simple starting procedure.

entry.title: A logic-based proof that shallow ReLU networks cannot compute maximum, with a witnessing refuter
entry.summary: A Witnessing Duality for ReLU Network Depth arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies depth lower bounds for ReLU networks computing the maximum function of n inputs, asking when a weak logical theory can prove such bounds. Working in the bounded arithmetic theory VTC^0, the authors prove for each fixed prime q and depth cap K the known bound for integer-weight networks, together with a refuter that outputs a polynomial-length rational input on which any shallower network errs. They also give a balanced construction meeting this threshold at n ≤ 2^K, and a rational family of depth O(log n / log log n).

entry.title: BudSplat: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting Under a Rendering Budget
entry.summary: BudSplat: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting under a Rendering Budget arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents BudSplat, a compact feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that keeps the most valuable Gaussians under a limited primitive count for novel view synthesis. It uses a detail-aware importance score from multi-level visual tokens and quality-aware pruning that jointly considers rendering contribution and detail importance. Experiments on RE10K, DL3DV, and ACID show a favorable trade-off between rendering quality and efficiency.

entry.title: Quantization's role in delayed loss spikes during language model pretraining
entry.summary: The Role of Quantization in Loss Spikes arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies time-bomb spikes, delayed training divergences that appear only after long pretraining and can waste substantial compute. The authors find that rising quantization error in the language modeling head precedes these spikes, with lower numerical precision accelerating them and higher precision improving stability. They propose replacing AdamW on the LM head with SGD with momentum to suppress logit growth, and note that existing mitigation techniques also reduce quantization error.

entry.title: NAGO: A flow-matching method that chooses a better noise source for sampling random physical fields
entry.summary: NAGO: Noise-Aware Generative Operator via Flow Matching arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces NAGO, a generative operator that treats the source distribution as a design choice rather than a fixed Gaussian, for sampling from invariant measures of stochastic PDEs in function space. It derives admissibility conditions and shows that the source-target covariance ratio controls spectral stiffness, leading to a rule that picks a sufficiently rough source and minimizes covariance mismatch over resolved Fourier modes. In a controlled Matern-field ablation, the accurate RK4 budget drops from about 30 steps for Gaussian functional flow matching to 3 to 5 steps.

entry.title: A hybrid neural network method for solving nonhomogeneous PDEs on complex domains
entry.summary: A Hybrid Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks Method arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a hybrid physics-informed holomorphic neural network (HPIHNN) framework that splits the solution into a particular part and a homogeneous part. The particular part is computed with a spectral method on a simple extended domain, while the homogeneous part is approximated by a network trained only on the boundary. The method is applied to nonhomogeneous Poisson, Stokes, biharmonic, linear elasticity, and Helmholtz equations. In the tested cases, it generally achieves lower errors and shorter training times than standard PINNs.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Abstractive Summarization for Marathi
entry.summary: Cross Lingual Abstractive Summarization for Marathi arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper builds cross-lingual training data for Marathi from the monolingual MahaSum corpus and the smaller PMIndiaSum dataset. It fine-tunes IndicTrans2, an Indic neural machine translation model, mainly for Marathi-to-English summarization. Evaluation uses ROUGE, chrF and chrF++ scores. The authors report that using a pretrained translation model performs substantially better than the IndicBART and mBART-50 baselines from earlier work.

entry.title: TreemapMix: Dirichlet-controlled multi-image augmentation for probability and ordinal supervision
entry.summary: TreemapMix: Dirichlet-Controlled Multi-Image Augmentation for Probability and Ordinal Supervision arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes TreemapMix, a data augmentation method that combines multiple images by sampling source weights from a Dirichlet distribution and assigning them to area-proportional regions via a treemap partition. The region areas serve as soft class-probability targets with soft cross-entropy (TreemapMix-SCE) or as ordinal supervision with a Plackett-Luce objective (TreemapMix-PL). On ImageNet-1K, TreemapMix-SCE achieves lower calibration error than evaluated mixed-sample baselines, while TreemapMix-PL achieves the highest Top-1 accuracy.

entry.title: ETA-Motion: efficient motion generation for any skeleton using sparse joints
entry.summary: ETA-Motion: Efficient Topology-Agnostic Motion Diffusion via Sparse Joint Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026ETA-Motion is a framework for generating motions for characters with arbitrary skeletal structures. It learns from a compact subset of joints rather than all joints, using semantic joint embeddings that combine text and visual cues along with topology-aware training objectives. The paper reports that it outperforms existing topology-agnostic baselines in efficiency and generalization to unseen motions and topologies, while still producing full-skeleton motions at inference.

entry.title: Learning Decision Policies from Mixed-Source Data When Hidden Confounders Exist
entry.summary: Transportable Offline Reinforcement Learning in Presence of Unmeasured Confounding arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies learning decision policies for a target domain from previously collected offline data, where source and target environments differ and some confounding variables are not measured. The authors combine transportability theory with instrumental variables, negative controls, and proxies, and propose CAT-CCB for confounded contextual bandits and CAT-CMDP for confounded Markov decision processes. They provide high-probability finite-sample suboptimality guarantees, and numerical experiments support the framework's effectiveness.

entry.title: Tutorial on generative models for music audio, covering methods for instrumental, song, editing, and live applications
entry.summary: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This monograph introduces, in a shared notation, the methods behind music audio generation, including neural audio codecs, autoregressive and masked token models, diffusion and flow matching, sampling acceleration, and preference optimization. It links training objectives and sampling procedures to published systems through worked examples. It also compares systems by representation, method, inputs, tasks, and release information, and discusses evaluation, listening tests, data provenance, memorization, and attribution. The authors note that differences in data, scale, and evaluation limit what cross-system comparisons can establish.

entry.title: Keepace.ai: A Large Language Model for Sports and Health, Technical Report
entry.summary: Keepace.ai: A Technical Report on a Large Language Model for Sports and Health arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This report presents Keepace.ai, a domain-specialized large language model built on Qwen3.5-27B through post-training and currently optimized for Chinese-language exercise guidance. It covers three tasks: workout plan generation, sports-and-health knowledge question answering, and personal sports data analysis. In internal rubric-based evaluations designed with domain experts, the model outperforms its base model and larger general-purpose baselines, most notably in exercise safety and scientific accuracy. The report also summarizes its design, data pipeline, safety-first evaluation framework, and results.

entry.title: Verification-Guided Retrosynthesis: How Checking Reactions During Search Improves Route Planning
entry.summary: Verification-Guided Retrosynthesis: Reaction Feedback and Evidence Timing arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to use reaction verification results to guide retrosynthesis route search. The authors introduce Verification-Guided Reflow (VGR), which treats reaction verification as a decision action within AND/OR search, pruning rejected reactions immediately and giving accepted reactions priority only when they form part of a complete candidate route. On Retro190, feedback raises verified solvability from 51.1% to 62.6%, and the delayed-guidance strategy further raises it to 71.1%.

entry.title: Precedent or Intent? How Coding Agents Choose Between Existing Code and New Instructions
entry.summary: Precedent or Intent? What Coding Agents Follow When Evolving Existing Code arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how coding agents decide whether to follow existing repository code or new task instructions when several implementations meet the same requirements. The authors ran 5,625 controlled trials across four coding agents and validated the findings in four open-source repositories. Agents overwhelmingly followed repository precedent over their defaults, and written priority rules achieved much higher success than code examples alone.

entry.title: IFAAB: An audit dataset checking whether AI financial advice in India varies by gender, caste and other social traits
entry.summary: The Indian Financial Automated Advice Bias (IFAAB) Dataset : Auditing Socioeconomic and Demographic Disparities in LLM-Generated Financial Advice in India arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces IFAAB, a dataset of 31,734 GPT-4o financial-advice responses generated for synthetic Indian personas differing in gender, caste, education, employment, residence, age and district. Using counterfactual comparisons, the authors find male-labelled profiles receive substantially higher implied post-advice total resources than comparable female-labelled profiles, a gap that shrinks when district is added. Caste-based differences are also reported, and women more often receive cautious saving advice while men more often receive growth-oriented advice.

entry.title: Offline RL that constrains policies by their state consequences
entry.summary: Variational Consequence-Driven Offline Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses offline reinforcement learning, where small action deviations can push an agent away from the offline dataset, by constraining policies through the state-consequence distributions they induce rather than action distributions alone. Because enforcing such constraints directly requires the true dynamics model, the authors propose Structural Behavior Regularization (StBR), which uses a closed-form latent divergence as a bounded surrogate. StBR tightens the behavior constraint adaptively in dynamics-sensitive regions and is reported to perform well across diverse offline RL benchmarks.

entry.title: 3DCodeEdit: A Benchmark for Instruction-Guided Editing of 3D Programs
entry.summary: 3DCodeEdit: Benchmarking Instruction-Guided 3D Program Editing arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces 3DCodeEdit, a benchmark of 2,592 editing tasks on 108 Blender programs that build 3D objects entirely in code. The edits range from parameter tweaks to structural, style, and scene changes, and are judged from renders against human-reviewed checklists. Across 17 models, the average success rate is 37%, and even the strongest models finish fewer than 60% of structural and style edits. The authors also find that multi-turn feedback from a separate reviewer model helps most in compensating for weak geometric foresight.

entry.title: A paper on speeding up FSDP training communication using zero-copy collectives on GPUs
entry.summary: The Endgame of FSDP Communication: Layout-Aware Collectives on Copy Engines, RDMA, and NVSwitch arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper addresses two costs in FSDP2 training: converting between per-parameter and flat buffer layouts, and communication kernels that slow concurrent compute. It presents TIDE, zero-copy collectives built on public NCCL 2.31+ APIs, with TIDE-AG delivering shards via NVSwitch multicast and RDMA, and TIDE-RS reducing bf16 gradients into fp32 shards. On 64 GPUs, TIDE reduces step time by up to 27.1% relative to Stock FSDP2.

entry.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Framework for Adaptive Forecasting from Mixed Evidence Sources
entry.summary: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents FACTS-MAS, a multi-agent forecasting framework that assigns different kinds of evidence, such as temporal dynamics, exogenous context, seasonality, and discrete events, to specialized agents. Each agent produces a forecast that is weighted by its skill on historical validation data, so uninformative evidence is downweighted or removed. Tested on Zillow housing inventory and FRED unemployment insurance claims for 15 U.S. metropolitan areas, it beats a naive last-value forecast and the TimesFM model, but matches a factor-adjusted exponential smoothing model.

entry.title: Silhouette-based gait analysis to assess frailty in older adults
entry.summary: Silhouette-Based Gaitomics for Frailty Assessment in Older Adults arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper uses body silhouette images from walking videos to extract gait features for assessing frailty in 66 older adults classified by the Fried Frailty Phenotype. The authors apply feature selection and explainable machine learning to link model predictions with measurable shape and motion patterns. CatBoost reached a mean three-class micro-AUC of 0.647, and frail versus nonfrail classification performed best, while separating prefrail from nonfrail participants was limited. The authors say larger independent studies are needed to establish reliability and clinical relevance.

entry.title: CuraEval: Testing Ways to Select Robot Training Demonstrations
entry.summary: CuraEval: Evaluating Demonstration Curation on Mixed-Skill Robot Data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces CuraEval, a framework for evaluating methods that select demonstrations for robot imitation learning. It compares these selection methods against size-matched random subsets and full-data training, using mixed-skill robomimic data with Diffusion Policy and BC-RNN. The results show that the selection methods' advantages are inconsistent, and after Holm correction no curated condition significantly outperforms full-data training.

entry.title: Rubricon: Automatically Generating and Refining Evaluation Rubrics for LLMs
entry.summary: Rubricon: Automated Rubric Generation and Refinement for LLM Evaluation and Training arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents Rubricon, a pipeline that automatically creates discriminative rubrics for scoring LLM responses on tasks without verifiable answers, without needing human preference labels. It samples several candidate rubrics, selects the most discriminative one, adds missing criteria, and removes misaligned ones. Across five benchmarks, its rubrics align about 9% better with expert-written rubrics than the best alternative synthetic method, and on HealthBench they improve post-training of a Qwen3.5-9B model by 4.5% over RRD-based rubrics.

entry.title: HotPOT: A Transformer with Mixed Physics Experts for Large-Scale PDE Pre-training
entry.summary: HotPOT: Operator Transformer with Heterogeneous Physics Experts for Large-Scale PDE Pre-training arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents HotPOT, a model for pre-training on many partial differential equations (PDEs) at once. A shared encoder captures information common to all PDEs, while each PDE family has its own expert that pairs a learnable predictor with a fixed numerical update computing the next state. Across five PDE families and six settings, HotPOT beats MoE-POT in all 24 matched-scale comparisons before and after fine-tuning, reducing rollout error by 50.7% on average. The gains also extend to zero-shot prediction under unseen physical conditions.

entry.title: Skeleton Coding: Using Program Structure as a Specification for AI Coding Agents
entry.summary: Skeleton Coding: Program Structure as a Specification for Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper argues that the program structure an AI coding agent chooses determines which tests are needed, so behavioral tests alone can leave a developer's intended program underdetermined. It introduces Skeleton Coding, where developers specify a high-level code-like structure alongside behavioral specifications. The authors show theoretically that skeletons can reduce the number of tests needed exponentially, and report that across four models and three benchmarks the best skeletons cut mean test error by 48.4% relative to the best end-to-end specifications.

entry.title: RainCheck: Using Historical Weather Data and Machine Learning to Forecast Rainfall in Bangladesh
entry.summary: RainCheck: Harnessing Historical Weather Data with Machine Learning for Rainfall Forecasting in Bangladesh arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This study uses 618,650 station-day records from 35 Bangladesh Meteorological Department stations, covering 1948 to 2014, to compare machine-learning rainfall forecasts. It finds that a station-month climatology alone classifies high-rainfall months with 88.4% accuracy, and most learners do not significantly beat climatology on future years. The authors also release a leakage-aware evaluation protocol and code.

entry.title: GAAC: Lossless compression of the LLM memory cache for faster on-device inference
entry.summary: GAAC: Lossless KV Compression for Bandwidth-Efficient LLM Inference on Personal Devices arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents GAAC, a lossless key-value (KV) cache compression and serving system for large language models that exploits redundancy in BF16 exponents without approximating the cached values. Across five tested models, it achieves 1.405 to 1.407 times lossless BF16 KV compression. On NVIDIA DGX Spark and Apple M4, it speeds up attention computation, with reported gains of 1.19 to 1.27 times at a 64K-token context and 1.02 to 1.25 times respectively.

entry.title: Progressive coupling diffusion sampling for reducing scan overlap in ptychography
entry.summary: Progressive Coupling Method for Diffusion Posterior Sampling in Ptychography arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Ptychography reconstructs a sample from overlapping diffraction measurements, but dense scanning makes acquisition slow. This paper proposes progressive coupling posterior sampling (PCPS), which explores the solution space broadly under high uncertainty and strengthens diffusion-guided consistency as reconstruction refines. Experiments on real X-ray ptychographic data at various scan overlaps show improved accuracy over traditional iterative methods and existing diffusion posterior samplers, especially at low overlaps. The results suggest diffusion priors can reduce the measurement redundancy needed for accurate reconstruction.

entry.title: Two Birds with One Stone: Unifying Skill Retrieval and Use in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Two Birds with One Stone: Skill-Augmented Generation via Unified Retrieval and Utilization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes Skill-Uni, a reinforcement learning framework in which a single language model learns both to retrieve reusable skills and to use them for solving tasks. Training uses a warm-up instruction tuning stage followed by GRPO. Across five skill-related benchmarks, it reports average gains of 66.59% over Qwen3-4B and 34.82% over LLaMA3.1-8B, and it works with various skill retrieval engines.

entry.title: From Natural Language to Real Schematics: Automated Power Electronics Circuit Design
entry.summary: From Natural Language to Real Schematics: An Automated Workflow for Power Electronics Schematic Synthesis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper presents a bounded dual-loop framework that converts natural language specifications into verified, editable KiCad schematics and manufacturing outputs. It covers Buck, Boost, Flyback, DAB, and half-bridge LLC topologies, using distributor APIs, datasheets, ngspice transient verification, and KiCad netlist round-trip checks. In two end-to-end case studies and comparisons with a Vanilla LLM baseline, component verification coverage, nominal value consistency, and SPICE simulation pass rates improved substantially.

entry.title: Embodied Underwater Intelligence: Imitation Learning for Multi-Task Underwater Manipulation
entry.summary: Embodied at Sea: Imitation Learning for Multi-Task Underwater Manipulation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper trains 14 generalist Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, called DynamicVLA, on 1616 underwater manipulation episodes collected in calm and turbulent waters to address visual distortion and currents underwater. Across three tasks, 10 models outperformed the baseline, and the best reached a 93.3% overall success rate. A marine archaeology case study compared a single-task Action Chunking Transformer with SmolVLA on grasping and mooring, with ACT substantially outperforming SmolVLA (47.9% vs. 7.9% pooled success). The BLUEMBODIED kit used for data collection, training, and deployment has been open sourced.

entry.title: Convex-SKM-Net: A low-latency method for enforcing convex constraints in neural networks via block halfspace corrections
entry.summary: Convex-SKM-Net: Low-Latency Block Halfspace Corrections for Neural Convex Constraint Satisfaction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces Convex-SKM-Net, a convex constraint-satisfaction layer that builds linearization halfspaces from residual and subgradient oracles and corrects predictions using fixed-depth dual projected-gradient descent on minimum-displacement block problems. The predictor and a positive-definite mobility matrix are learned jointly to improve objective quality. Reported tests on second-order-cone model-predictive control and power-system convex relaxations keep outputs within a 10^-3 feasibility tolerance, with inference speedups of up to 144.3 times over compared methods.

entry.title: GearUp: DAG-aware serverless inference acceleration via slack-guided pre-loading
entry.summary: GearUp: DAG-aware Acceleration for Serverless Inference Serving via Slack-guided Pre-loading arXiv · Oct 28, 2026GearUp is a serverless system for running machine learning inference workflows structured as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). It schedules each node's library, model weight, and CUDA kernel loading within the slack time the DAG exposes, hiding initialization behind upstream execution. The system also reuses initialized instances and uses a traffic-adaptive keep-alive policy. On the AMBER Alert and FINRA-ML workflows, it reduces median end-to-end latency by 64.5% and 75.9% compared with SMIless.

entry.title: A benchmark and prototype-guided method for detecting surface defects on shampoo bottles across many product variants
entry.summary: Prototype-Guided Dynamic Domain Modulation and a Large-Scale Multi-SKU Benchmark for Shampoo Bottle Surface Defect Detection arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses shampoo bottle surface defect detection, where the same defect can look different across product variants (SKUs). The authors introduce Bottle-SKU, a benchmark with 13,119 images, 20,419 bounding boxes, seven defect categories, and 48 bottle SKUs. They propose ProDMM, which builds a visual prototype for each SKU and uses it to dynamically modulate a Grounding DINO detector while keeping its pretrained detection path. Experiments on Bottle-SKU and the public GC10-DET-SKU dataset are reported to show the approach's effectiveness.

entry.title: Adding Multimodal Grounding to Text Moderation for Detecting Fraudulent Inducement in Short Videos
entry.summary: Complementing Text Based Moderation with Multimodal Grounding: Detecting Fraudulent Inducement Behaviors on Short Video Platforms arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses fraudulent inducement behaviors on short video platforms, such as prompts to like, follow, or join private chat groups. It compares three approaches: OCR+LLM, OCR+MLLM, and a large zero-shot multimodal LLM, using a dataset of 2,419 videos with 3,194 annotated events. The OCR+MLLM method localizes offending segments better than the keyframe-based baseline (mIoU 26.52 vs. 14.49) and detects non-textual inducements that text-only pipelines miss. It maintains 67.0 percent macro recall.

entry.title: In-context learning for multi-fidelity multiscale model closure and cross-operator generalization
entry.summary: In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework that uses one shared model to learn multiple multi-fidelity operators. The model takes paired low- and high-fidelity examples from multiple PDE operators as demonstrations, plus a new coarse-scale solution query, and predicts the corresponding fine-scale solution. After training, it predicts fine-scale solutions for a new operator from fewer than five coarse-fine demonstration pairs and a low-cost coarse query, without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Scaling Lean Theorem Proving for Real-World Code Verification
entry.summary: Scaling Lean Theorem Proving for Real-World Code Verification arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper presents EasyProver, a Lean proving system built from recursive agents, asynchronous search, and parallel tactic probing, which uses an off-the-shelf model without additional training to solve most problems on benchmarks such as PutnamBench and IMO 2026 formalizations. Because these benchmarks are near saturation, the authors introduce Aegis, which turns competitive programming problems into harder verification tasks over real Rust implementations translated to Lean. The pipeline yields 2,045 differentially validated Rust-Lean program pairs and 11,533 candidate specifications. On a stratified sample of 2,000 statements, EasyProver proves 1,054 (52.7%) within a 30-minute budget per statement.

entry.title: Gradient-Based Adversarial Augmentation for Countering Unlearnable Datasets
entry.summary: A Gradient based Adversarial Augmentation Framework for Mitigating Unlearnable Datasets arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a gradient-based adversarial augmentation framework for stress-testing unlearnable data methods (ULD), which add imperceptible perturbations to public data to block unauthorized model training. The framework learns an augmentation policy via stochastic gradient ascent over a differentiable pipeline of up to 18 augmentation techniques, training to maximize a surrogate model's classification loss. A perceptual-plus-pixel regularization preserves image semantics. Under a controlled ablation, it outperforms an equivalent random sampling baseline.

entry.title: Uneven data sizes across sites improve federated learning for brain imaging
entry.summary: Data Amount Heterogeneity Improves Performance in Federated Learning for Neuroimaging arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies federated learning for neuroimaging, specifically classifying Alzheimer's disease from structural MRI scans. It compares federations where sites have unequal data amounts (one large site plus small sites) against federations where every site holds the same amount of data. The heterogeneous federations perform better, especially in low-data settings, and come close to centralized training. A large site often leads to faster convergence and higher final accuracy.

entry.title: B2P-Corr: Batch-to-population gradient estimators for correlation losses that cannot be split across mini-batches
entry.summary: B2P-Corr: Batch-to-Population Gradient Estimators for Non-Decomposable Correlation Losses arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper observes that correlation metrics such as Pearson and concordance correlation depend on dataset-wide statistics, so naive mini-batch training yields biased, high-variance gradients. It proposes B2P-Corr, which converts these objectives into decomposable pseudo-losses using lightweight global moment sketches, with two variants, B2P-EMA and B2P-U. Experiments on two synthetic and three real-world datasets show more stable optimization and higher correlation than naive mini-batch training, with negligible overhead.

entry.title: Replaying Gradients at a Different ε: A Pre-Registered Test of Adam's ε Explanation for a Rare Embedding Row
entry.summary: Replaying the Same Gradients at a Different ǎrepsilon: A Registered Test of the Fixed-Trajectory Account of Adam's ǎrepsilon for One Rare Row arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper examines how Adam's epsilon term affects updates to a rare token's output-embedding row. During training, the authors recompute that row's updates with a different epsilon while keeping the gradients fixed, and test this explanation against a rule written before the runs. When epsilon rises by four orders of magnitude, the replay predictions are clearly wrong, with the row keeping far more of its displacement than predicted. At three orders of magnitude the gap is smaller and less clear.

entry.title: Neighbourhood shortcuts in satellite building damage assessment, with a building-evidence plug-in to reduce them
entry.summary: Neighbourhood shortcuts in building damage assessment from very-high-resolution satellite imagery: diagnosis and a building-evidence plug-in arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines deep models that assess building damage from very-high-resolution satellite imagery and finds they often rely on neighbouring buildings' damage levels as a shortcut, missing isolated damaged buildings. The authors propose a plug-in that adds two experts to an existing model without retraining it, one looking only at the building and one trained to ignore swapped neighbourhoods. The plug-in is reported to reduce neighbourhood-driven errors across nine models.

entry.title: ATI-OPD: Adaptive Teacher Intervention for Stable Long-Sequence On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary: ATI-OPD: Adaptive Teacher Intervention for Stable Long-Sequence On-Policy Distillation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes ATI-OPD, a training method that improves on-policy distillation, where a student learns from its own responses using token-level feedback from a teacher. For long responses, the student's reasoning prefix can drift from the teacher's, weakening later feedback and destabilizing training. ATI-OPD replaces the earliest high-disagreement segment with a short teacher segment and lets the student resume reasoning from the revised text. Across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two teacher-student pairs, it improves average student-only accuracy over standard on-policy distillation.

entry.title: REEL: Same frames, different answers and costs
entry.summary: REEL: Same Frames, Different Answers and Different Costs arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces REEL, an evaluation framework that compares three saved memories built from the same video frames: a text record, visual encoder outputs, and language-model prefix state. Each is compared against reprocessing the full frames using paired correctness changes, cumulative GPU time, and storage size. Across six vision-language models and two benchmarks, Text differs from Frames on 20% to 29% of questions despite similar mean accuracy, while Prefix State stays closest to Frames and has the lowest total GPU time, at the cost of up to about 21 GiB per video.

entry.title: Simulating creator ecosystems to test fair video recommendation allocation at billion-user scale
entry.summary: Floor It, Then Fill It: Simulating Creator Ecosystems for Fair Video-Content Recommendation Systems at Billion User Scale arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a user-simulation framework that models about 42,000 creators and their viewer interactions over 12 weeks, grounded in real platform distributions. It evaluates equitable view-allocation policies formulated as a budgeted multi-armed bandit, varying view targets, reward functions, and a small-creator reserve. A floor-protected approach meets 90% of view targets weekly and raises small-creator organic reach by about 33% per week.

entry.title: MASS: A multi-mask selective self-distillation method for leakage-resilient reasoning (paper)
entry.summary: MASS: Multi-mask Selective Self-Distillation for Leakage-Resilient Reasoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes MASS, a multi-mask selective self-distillation method for improving reasoning in language models. It creates multiple independently masked views of one verified solution so the teacher model can combine diverse reference signals, then selectively transfers reliable token-level corrections while focusing masking on influential reference spans. Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks and several model families show that MASS consistently outperforms strong self-distillation baselines.

entry.title: StepControl: Generating Long Human Motion from Foot-Contact Timing Schedules
entry.summary: StepControl: Long-Horizon Human Motion Generation from Foot-Contact Schedules arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces StepControl, an autoregressive diffusion model that generates full-body human motion from a schedule specifying when each foot touches the ground. It needs no target root or body poses and no semantic prompts, representing contact as explicit temporal events injected via cross-attention with classifier-free guidance. Experiments show it follows prescribed contact timing more accurately than adapted spatially guided generators, and keeps control over long rollouts and edited schedules such as cadence changes, pauses, limping, and jumping.

entry.title: Estimating Implicit Expected Log Density Ratios: a study introducing the expected log density ratio (ELDR) and its finite-sample estimation limits
entry.summary: Estimating Implicit Expected Log Density Ratios arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces the expected log density ratio (ELDR), which is the integral of log density ratios under a third measure. It shows that many implicit-density problems that naively use density ratio estimation (DRE) are actually ELDR estimation tasks. The authors prove fundamental limits on finite-sample ELDR estimation and argue that typical DRE methods are unsuitable for it. They also propose a simple modification to some DRE methods, which benchmarks show can reduce ELDR estimation error.

entry.title: SkillCT: A multi-dimensional benchmark and execution-free baseline for rating AI agent skills
entry.summary: SkillCT: A Multidimensional Benchmark and Execution-Free Baseline for Agent Skill Assessment arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces SkillCT, a benchmark that assesses agent skills across nine dimensions grouped into static, dynamic, and human-assisted assessment, going beyond task execution success. It also proposes an execution-free baseline that predicts a skill's quality profile by retrieving similar reference skills. According to the authors, this approach lowers token use and evaluation time, and SkillCT-guided optimization improves downstream task success and execution efficiency.

entry.title: El Agente Quntur: AI agents choosing active spaces for CASSCF chemistry calculations
entry.summary: El Agente Quntur: Agentic Active-Space Selection for CASSCF arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper tests whether a multi-agent AI system can reliably choose the active orbital space for CASSCF multireference quantum chemistry calculations. The agents selected orbitals, checked target excited states, and judged convergence for 32 singlet excitations, and their results were compared with six fixed Active Space Finder protocols using published CASPT2 reference values. The agentic approach reduced mean absolute error by 48% relative to the best deterministic protocol. The authors also note that computational traces and costs varied substantially across runs, even for the same molecule.

entry.title: Decompose, Don't Expand: Designing AI systems that work regardless of model size
entry.summary: Decompose, Don't Expand: Capability-Independent AI Systems by Construction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines a design choice in AI systems: when a task is too hard for a model, expand the model or decompose the task so a deterministic host handles the solvable parts and the model handles only the fuzzy remainder. The authors report measurements across nine models, finding that on the extracted sub-tasks performance no longer varies with model size. They argue the approach is a general design discipline applicable to physics setup, motion retargeting, and object-model editing.

entry.title: A Separation Principle for Attacks and Defenses on Graph Neural Networks
entry.summary: A Separation Principle for Adversarial Attacks and Defense of Graph Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper treats adversarial attacks on graph neural networks as a problem shaped by graph structure, not only by gradients or learned policies. It derives feature attacks from the spectral properties of the normalized adjacency operator and states a separation principle: the optimal perturbation is rank one, splitting into a graph-dependent degree-based allocation and a weight-dependent top singular vector. Based on this, the authors propose SepAttack, a gradient-free attack, and SepAT, an adversarial training procedure.

entry.title: MiniMMD: Minimizing MMD for Sampling, Inference and Integration
entry.summary: MiniMMD: Minimization of MMD for Sampling, Inference and Integration arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This thesis presents a unified approach to many problems in statistics and machine learning, which approximate a target distribution by minimizing the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), a kernel-based distance between probability distributions. It argues that MMD is both a statistically meaningful distance and a tractable objective for designing practical, efficient algorithms. The thesis summarizes recent theoretical and empirical advances in these minimum-MMD-based algorithms.

entry.title: Too Hard, Too Easy, Just Right: Adaptive Challenge in VR Firefighter Training
entry.summary: Too Hard, Too Easy, Just Right: Performance-Driven Challenge Adaptation in Virtual Reality Firefighter Training arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents ProACT, a performance-driven adaptive training system for virtual reality firefighter training. It adjusts scenario difficulty through closed-loop interaction between trainee performance and simulated fire dynamics. A global module updates scene-level fire spread in real time, while a local module periodically updates object-level flammability. Compared with adaptive and non-adaptive baselines, ProACT improves both objective training performance and subjective user experience.

entry.title: Beauty Is Human: Liking AI Art Leads People to Think a Human Made It
entry.summary: Beauty Is Human: When People Love AI-Generated Art, They Think a Human Made It arXiv · Oct 28, 2026In a public online AI Art Turing Test, 11,123 people judged whether 50 pictures, 26 of them AI-generated, were made by humans and picked their favourites. Holding respondent and picture fixed, a picture was 22.1 percentage points more likely to be judged human-made when it was the respondent's favourite, with a similar pattern for AI-generated and human-made favourites. A reanalysis of a published AI poetry experiment found the same pattern, suggesting that when provenance is hidden, liking and perceived human authorship go together.

entry.title: From Gettier Machine to Justified True Output: Rational Trust in Generative AI
entry.summary: From the Gettier Machine to Justified True Output: A Three-Step Account of Rational Trust in Generative AI arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper asks when a user who takes a proposition from generative AI output actually knows it and when trusting it is rational. It argues that failures of AI-mediated inquiry match the problems that the justified-true-belief tradition and its post-Gettier anti-luck refinements were built to diagnose. It proposes a three-step pattern of use (acquisition, understanding, independent verification) and a stakes-indexed criterion called justified true output (JTO), with the everyday test: "Had this been false, would I have noticed?"

entry.title: Who Called? V33DA: A Verified Multimodal Benchmark for Identifying Zebra Finch Callers
entry.summary: Who Called? V33DA: A Physically Verified Multimodal Benchmark for Vocal Attribution in Zebra Finch Groups arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces V33DA, a benchmark dataset for determining which zebra finch in a group produced a vocalization and where it was made. It contains 33,625 events that pair multichannel audio, three camera views, calibrated 3D bird poses, and radio telemetry for 10 birds, with caller identity verified by an on-body accelerometer that is withheld from the models. The authors test methods under three regimes and find that approaches relying on familiar vocal identity perform well on known birds but degrade on unseen ones, while candidate-aware spatial methods transfer better. The dataset, evaluation protocols, and code are released publicly.

entry.title: TGTV: An Interpretable Framework for Drone Fault Detection and Tracing Using Graph Learning and LLMs
entry.summary: TGTV: An Interpretable Framework for UAV Fault Detection and Traceability via Spatiotemporal Graph Learning and Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents TGTV, a framework for detecting and tracing faults in fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles. It combines spatiotemporal graph learning with a large language model, using temporal and graph networks plus a Transformer-VAE to flag anomalies and continuous-time Shapley attribution to identify critical sensors and intervals. On the public ALFA dataset with cross-flight holdout, it reports a window-level PR-AUC of 0.976 and a flight-level fault diagnosis F1 score of 0.944.

entry.title: Same Label, Different Interface: Robot Learning Action Labels Hide Key Differences
entry.summary: Same Label, Different Interface: Beyond Action-Space Labels in Robot Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Robot-learning studies often compare position and velocity actions as if the label alone defined the experimental condition. This paper tests five joint-space interfaces on three contact-rich Factory tasks (PegInsert, GearMesh, NutThread) under one shared learner and training budget. It finds that omitted properties such as physical action scale, filtering, and feedback affect results, and that even a calibrated velocity scale leaves residual performance gaps.

entry.title: The Prestige: A Benchmark for Visual Reasoning Using Magic Tricks
entry.summary: The Prestige: Benchmarking Cognitive Visual Reasoning using Magic Tricks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces The Prestige, a video understanding benchmark built from professional magic performances that use deliberate misdirection. It tests models on tracking events and explaining unexpected outcomes, with open-ended questions covering temporal and causal reasoning and robustness to adversarial questions. Evaluations of leading vision-language models show a substantial gap between even the strongest model and human performance.

entry.title: An AI-driven digital twin framework that optimizes warehouse automation
entry.summary: AI-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Warehouse Logistics Automation Optimization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a framework in which a reinforcement learning agent, operating within a FlexSim-based digital twin, optimizes product placement in real time. The agent learns continuously from streaming operational data to reduce picking time and raise throughput. The simulated environment models a four-zone warehouse with forklift handling and uses the Asset Administration Shell framework to link the agent, physical asset, and digital twin. Reported results show a 29.66% drop in average picking time, a 35.42% throughput increase, and an 18.54% reduction in travel distance.

entry.title: Testing Whether LLMs Really Reason Causally: A Case Study on CLadder Benchmark Shortcuts
entry.summary: Evaluating Causal Reasoning in LLMs: A Case Study in the Challenges of Procedural Generation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines what can reliably be concluded when large language models perform well on test sets generated by the CLadder benchmark framework. The authors find that the generator embeds superficial, highly predictive patterns, and even simple random forest models perform well on its data. They also show that many commercial LLMs are brittle on these test sets, with performance barely changing when text critical for formal causal reasoning is removed. The authors argue that strong LLM results most likely reflect exploitation of these surface patterns.

entry.title: Language models' limit calculations and feasibility rejections diverge under mechanical tests
entry.summary: Calculation and rejection diverge in language models tested at known mechanical limits arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper tests 12 language models on engineering problems such as beam loads and disk speeds set above or below known plastic collapse or burst limits. Across 4,860 calls and follow-up experiments on new designs, it finds that models can reject impossible designs when asked only about feasibility, yet may accept the same designs and report them as solved when asked for a full answer. Some models accepted beams exceeding collapse limits despite calculating those limits correctly in separate questions.

entry.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning: Open, efficient AI models for agent tasks
entry.summary: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models for Agentic AI arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces Nemotron 3.5 Super, a 120B-parameter multimodal model with 12B active parameters, and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B-parameter text model with 3B active parameters, both built for reasoning, long-context tasks, and agentic workloads. The models combine large-scale distillation, long-context training, and native speculative decoding, and Super adds Indic pretraining and software-engineering mid-training. After post-training with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, the post-trained Super model reaches 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro, and inference optimizations reach up to 4,856 output tokens/s/GPU on GB200.

entry.title: What Firms Can Do About Model Distillation: an economic analysis of distillation attacks and countermeasures.
entry.summary: What Can Firms Do in the Face of Model Distillation? arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper examines how smaller firms can distill training data from conversations with powerful closed-weight AI models to build their own models at much lower cost. Using a two-player model of an incumbent and a distilling competitor, it studies effects on market competition, user surplus, and the incumbent's utility. It finds that penalty-based regulation can fully deter distillation when attacks are detectable, though it may harm competition and users, while self-distillation can mitigate undetectable attacks and help preserve competition.

entry.title: From Next-Day to Multi-Day Wildfire Spread: A New Multi-Continent Active-Fire Dataset for Sequence Forecasting
entry.summary: From Next Day Wildfire to Next Days Wildfire: A New Multi-Continent Dataset of Active-Fire Spread for Sequence-to-Sequence Forecasting arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces AFSeq, a multimodal dataset of 1,194 fire events from 2023 to 2026 across eight countries in three regions, focusing on short, small fires that existing benchmarks underrepresent. It also presents UTAE-AR, a U-Net-based model with a Temporal Auto Encoder and recurrent modules that forecasts a whole sequence autoregressively by feeding its predicted fire masks back day by day. The authors report that UTAE-AR outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods on next-day accuracy across WSTS, WSTS+ and AFSeq while using about 21.5% of their parameters.

entry.title: Finding Interpretable Features in Text Using LLM Comparisons and Choice Models
entry.summary: Interpretable Feature Discovery from Unstructured Data Using LLMs and Statistical Choice Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes a method that has large language models compare pairs of items and explain in interpretable terms what distinguishes them, then uses a statistical choice model to combine these explanations into relevant features and per-item feature scores. On a synthetic hiring dataset of cover letters with known ground-truth features, the method significantly outperforms direct LLM feature extraction in recovering those features. On the ChangeMyView Reddit debate dataset, it discovers several features associated with persuasion while reaching predictive accuracy comparable to established baselines.

entry.title: Testing Monocular Depth Estimation for Lunar Surface Imagery
entry.summary: Efficacy of Monocular Depth Estimation in Lunar Environments arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper tests how well several state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation methods work on lunar terrain, which lies outside the terrestrial data they were trained on. The authors use the NASA Ames POLAR stereo dataset and Apollo 17 surface images, comparing results against ground-truth physical analogs and historical field data. They report that some of these techniques can generalize to produce high-fidelity relative 3D reconstructions of the unstructured lunar surface.

entry.title: Neural compression of long ADMM trajectories for solving multiparametric quadratic programs
entry.summary: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents TQPNet, a self-supervised neural framework that compresses long ADMM optimization trajectories into a compact neural warm start followed by a few refinement iterations. The network combines a ReLU multilayer perceptron with unrolled ADMM(ReLU) refinement layers and is trained offline using an optimality-condition residual loss, without solver-generated labels. Experiments on large-scale multiparametric quadratic programs and real-time model predictive control show high accuracy, strong generalization, and much faster inference than conventional optimization methods.

entry.title: Prompt Lottery: How Rewording a Judge Prompt Can Change LLM Evaluation Results
entry.summary: Prompt Lottery in LLM-as-a-Judge: Measuring and Mitigating Sensitivity to Syntactic Rephrasing arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies whether using a large language model as an evaluator gives consistent judgments when the judge prompt is reworded without changing its meaning. The authors name the effect "Prompt Lottery," showing that paraphrased prompts can change evaluation outcomes and, in some settings, reverse model rankings. A user study with 10 human annotators compares agreement under rephrasing, and the authors show that aggregating judgments across multiple prompt variants improves robustness.

entry.title: From Error Prediction to Causal Influence: Auditing SAE Features in Multiple-Choice QA
entry.summary: From Error Prediction to Causal Influence: Auditing SAE Features in Multiple-Choice QA arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether sparse autoencoder (SAE) features that predict model errors also causally influence answers in multiple-choice question answering. Using Gemma 3 1B and 4B with Gemma Scope SAEs across eight datasets, the authors filter out features tied to prompt and answer-order artifacts before testing causal interventions. SAE activations predict wrongness and uncertainty, and the filtered features shift answer margins more than random features, yet answer flips are rare and effects are inconsistent across meaning-preserving changes. The features therefore appear to reflect context-dependent answer competition rather than the mechanism behind incorrect answers.

entry.title: Coordinating EV Charging Across Stations with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: QMIX vs. Independent Q-Learning
entry.summary: Cooperative EV Charging Assignment Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: A Comparison of QMIX and Independent Q-Learning Under Urban Traffic Uncertainty arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper models the assignment of electric vehicles to several charging stations as a decentralized partially observable decision problem and compares QMIX, a centralized-training method, with an independent Q-learning baseline. Tested on a six-station urban network simulated in SUMO under four traffic flow levels, QMIX achieved higher mean reward and acceptance rate. An ablation study suggests the gain comes mainly from the training architecture rather than the cooperative reward terms or experience sharing.

entry.title: Conformal prediction distributions for contextual order-fulfillment optimization
entry.summary: Conformal Predictive Distributions for Contextual Order Fulfillment Optimization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper builds conformal predictive distributions for delivery time using Conformal Predictive Systems for regression and the cross Venn-Abers predictor for multiclass classification. These distributions feed a contextual optimization model for choosing fulfillment locations and carriers, solved with contextual sample-average approximation. On over five million proprietary order records, CVAP raised exact-day accuracy from 49.5% to 64.1%. In simulator experiments over six test dates, the methods reduced mean total cost by 7.1% and 6.7% and cut the late-delivery rate from 5.7% to below 4.0%.

entry.title: Classifying Urban Locations by Cyclist Facility Use and Travel Direction
entry.summary: Classifying Urban Locations by Cyclist Facility Usage and Directional Alignment: A Validated Camera-Based Framework from Multi-Site Observations arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The study analyzes footage from motion-triggered cameras at 17 locations in Tempe, Arizona, in 2023 to see how cyclists use bike lanes and sidewalks. It finds that higher bike lane usage is associated with less wrong-way riding (Spearman rho = -0.87). Deployments are classified as bike-lane dominant, sidewalk dominant, or mixed.

entry.title: PromptSense: A Mental Health Chatbot That Adjusts Its Prompts Based on Detected Emotion
entry.summary: PromptSense: Sentiment-Aware Mental Health Chatbot with Dynamic Prompting arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a framework that analyzes sentiment and depression before model inference, applies a rule-based filter, and dynamically builds prompts from the results. It aims to make responses from mental health chatbots built on large language models more contextually relevant, empathetic, and risk-aware. The authors compared four model strategies and two prompt-engineered variants on qualitative measures such as empathy and safety, plus toxicity scores from the Perspective API. The prompt engineering approaches outperformed DSFT and RLAIF by 1.8% and 1.1%, respectively.

entry.title: Can Event Detectors Work Beyond Broadcast Cameras? A Tennis Study
entry.summary: Can Event Detectors Leave the Broadcast Camera? Evidence from Tennis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper releases a tennis benchmark of 345 frame-level annotations of ball bounces and racket hits across eight clips from broadcast, fixed elevated, phone and court-level viewpoints. It compares supervised spotters trained on broadcast footage, two zero-shot vision-language models, and RallyArb, a rule-based arbitration method that fits no parameters on event labels. Supervised spotters perform near-perfectly on broadcast video but poorly on phone and court-level footage.

entry.title: CARF: A Framework Using Expert-Corrected Reasoning to Screen Scientific Evidence
entry.summary: CARF: Context-Aware Reasoning Supervision for Scientific Evidence Screening arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces CARF, a human-in-the-loop framework that adapts language models to screening studies for systematic reviews by learning from expert feedback on their generated reasoning. Systematic reviews require experts to manually screen thousands of studies against eligibility criteria. The authors evaluated CARF on reviews of verbal autopsy and cause-of-death methods used in global public health mortality surveillance. CARF showed competitive screening performance with high sensitivity and was more inclined to keep ambiguous, context-dependent studies for human review.

entry.title: EARS-Info: Information-Aware Event-Driven Reallocation for Multi-Robot Exploration
entry.summary: EARS-Info: Information-Aware Event-Driven Reallocation for Multi-Robot Exploration arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents EARS-Info, an information-aware extension of Event-Driven Ant Reallocation Search for multi-robot exploration on grids derived from OpenStreetMap. Across 168,000 episodes on eight city maps, it achieved the highest mean operational score in every evaluation panel. With eight robots and 3% communication dropout, it improved the score over EARS-Safe by 5.43% and raised weighted discovery from 88.88% to 98.46%.

entry.title: Faster deep Gaussian process surrogates using mini-batch latent MAP estimation
entry.summary: Efficient Deep Gaussian Process Surrogates via Mini-Batch Latent MAP Estimation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes the latent maximum-a-posteriori deep Gaussian process (LaMP-DGP), which uses gradient-based optimization to estimate latent representations and performs probabilistic prediction through linked-GP calculations. To scale to large datasets, the authors develop a mini-batch optimization algorithm and establish a stationarity bound for latent-state optimization. Experiments report predictive performance competitive with several existing inference methods, and substantially faster computation than the Vecchia MCMC approach.

entry.title: Measuring Deep Learning Performance: How Results Vary Across Architectures and Tasks
entry.summary: Measuring Deep Learning Performance - An Empirical Study of Performance Distributions Across Architectures and Tasks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This study examines how deep learning model performance varies due to randomness, using 186 experiments with 100 random seeds each, totaling 18,600 runs, across image classification and time series forecasting. Performance distributions are often non-Gaussian, and time series models produce nearly three times more underperforming outliers than image classification models. The authors conclude that mean performance alone is insufficient for model selection, and that spread, symmetry, and tail risk should also be assessed.

entry.title: Learning from relative action credit to escape local minima in robot reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Learning from Relative Action Credit for Escaping Local Minima arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses why on-policy methods like PPO often stall on long-horizon, contact-rich robot manipulation tasks. The authors argue that state-value critics judge progress only by episode outcomes, so they cannot distinguish better actions once the policy reaches a partial solution. They extend PPO with an action-conditioned value critic that compares the executed action with alternatives sampled at the same state, combined with Generalized Advantage Estimation and a bound on exploration noise. The extended method escapes the plateau and completes precise peg insertion within a training budget where PPO with identical exploration fails.

entry.title: Metatron: A Promptable Whole-Body Execution Layer for Humanoid Robots
entry.summary: METATRON: A Promptable Whole-Body Execution Layer for Humanoids arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents Metatron, a whole-body control layer for humanoid robots that pairs a generative base policy with a programmable skill layer. The base policy takes partial goals, such as timed body-part targets, velocity commands, and style cues, and produces diverse whole-body motions that match them. After training, the policy is frozen, and skills written as code issue prompts at each control step. On a physical Unitree G1, one frozen checkpoint supports walking, recovery, teleoperated object pickup, and sitting on furniture, with higher reaching success and push robustness than the tested reference-tracking pipelines.

entry.title: How Users Explain Audience Change: Causal Attribution and Boundary Management on Xiaohongshu
entry.summary: Making Sense of Audience Change: Causal Attribution and Boundary Management on Xiaohongshu arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines Xiaohongshu discussions about a perceived audience influx linked to the World Cup, studying how users explained community change and how those explanations related to boundary-management strategies. The authors analyzed 262 comments from eight high-engagement threads. They found that algorithmic explanations were mostly tied to technical boundary management, while explanations centered on social actors more often aligned with social enforcement or normative socialization.

entry.title: Testing whether language models can handle fusion physics questions
entry.summary: Assessing Language Models for Scientific Applications: Inertial Confinement Fusion as a Use Case arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper evaluates language models on inertial confinement fusion using a 250-question benchmark covering qualitative reasoning, numerical calculation, symbolic derivation, and equation formulation. It compares general models with Prospero, a model specialized for ICF through domain pretraining and fine-tuning, and tests retrieval-assisted answering. Prospero improved its aggregate score by 10.7 percentage points over its base model, while frontier models scored highest but still made critical physics errors in numerical calculations.

entry.title: Detecting brain tumour progression from wearable accelerometer signatures
entry.summary: Detecting Brain Cancer Progression Through Signatures of Wearable Accelerometry Data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This study examines patients with high-grade gliomas, using wrist-worn accelerometer recordings of walking converted into path segments. It applies rough path signatures and signature kernel maximum mean discrepancy to measure changes in walking behaviour. Normalising each patient against their own stable-period variation improved separation between stable and progressive disease. The authors present proof-of-concept evidence and call for larger longitudinal studies.

entry.title: Beyond Aggregate WER: Domain Adaptation and Learner Speech in Spanish Classroom ASR
entry.summary: Beyond Aggregate WER: In-domain Adaptation, Learner Speech, Code-Switching, and Speaker Attribution in Online Spanish Learning Classrooms arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper evaluates automatic speech recognition on online L2 Spanish classes where English-speaking learners interact with instructors and tutors. It compares platform, open-weight, adapted, and commercial systems, and adapts Whisper and MOSS with LoRA using human-corrected classroom data. Domain match mattered more than data volume, and learner, English-only, and code-switched speech remained harder to recognize than instructor and Spanish-only speech.

entry.title: When Model-Derived Measurements Can Be Corrected or Compared
entry.summary: Measured or Real? When Model-Derived Measurements Can Be Corrected or Compared arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies numbers computed from trained models, such as example difficulty or benchmark leads, which change with random seed and prompt. It shows that the textbook correlation correction can return values above one and proposes correcting only when both reliabilities pass a significance test, dividing by their upper confidence bounds. It also reports that prompt settings can reverse model rankings and compares models within each prompt setting.

entry.title: Transferable black-box attacks on MLLMs guided by semantic vulnerability (VISTA)
entry.summary: Where Can We Fool the Model's Mind? Response-Guided Semantic Probing and Adaptive Routing for Transferable Attacks on Black-Box MLLMs arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents VISTA, a black-box framework that finds semantically vulnerable image regions from an multimodal LLM's responses and focuses adversarial perturbations there, without using gradients, logits, or parameters. It offers VISTA-Proxy, which probes an open-source model and transfers examples to commercial models without querying them, and VISTA-Victim, which queries the target model. The authors report attack success rates up to 97% on GPT-5, Gemini-3.5-Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 while keeping PSNR above 30 dB. VISTA-Proxy reaches up to 93% success without querying the final victim.

entry.title: Statistical mechanics of scale-invariant learning: spectral equations of state and curvature transport
entry.summary: Finite-step statistical mechanics of scale-invariant learning: spectral equations of state and curvature transport arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies thermodynamic-like relations in discrete stochastic gradient learning dynamics that follow from scale symmetry rather than equilibrium assumptions. It explains an entropy-scaling relation through an exact rescaling of trajectories and derives a spectral equation of state whose virial coefficients depend on curvature-spectrum moments under a local harmonic approximation. The authors also present an exact curvature-transport identity for quantifying deviations from the ideal-gas description, tested on sphere models, teacher-student networks, and convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

entry.title: Using large language models to accurately extract information from medical charts for stroke research
entry.summary: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper evaluates a prompting-based large language model framework for extracting eight clinical variables from 2,416 acute stroke intervention reports across three hospitals. Twenty-two open-source models were compared, and LLaMA3.3-70B with Chain-of-Thought prompting achieved the highest overall accuracy at 94.8%. The authors conclude that locally deployed LLMs can support scalable clinical data extraction and stroke registry curation, with expert oversight for ambiguous cases.

entry.title: Making Smart Homes Suit Autistic Children: Family Work and Monitored Independence
entry.summary: Making Smart Homes Fit for Autistic Children: Family Work and Monitored Independence arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This qualitative study examines how general-purpose smart-home technologies affect autistic children and their families, drawing on five caregiver interviews and posts from Xiaohongshu and Weibo. Families adapt environmental outputs, prompts, and interaction channels to create support, while sensory intensity, communication rules, and opaque operating states can turn the same technologies into barriers. Remote monitoring enables conditional independence but creates tensions among safety, privacy, and control.

entry.title: Frequency-adaptive Gaussian grids for compact image representation
entry.summary: Frequency-Adaptive Gaussian Grids for Efficient Image Representation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces Gaussian-Grid, a hybrid neural image representation that combines structured feature grids with unstructured 2D Gaussians. It divides computation between the two based on local frequency content, adapting its architecture to the complexity of each image. On high-resolution natural images, it reports 1.24 to 2.14 times faster decoding and 23 to 176 times lower PCIe data traffic than JPEG plus ZIP archiving, while keeping memory use small and reconstruction fidelity high.

entry.title: Healthcare Professionals' Views on Algorithmic Bias in Medical AI
entry.summary: Algorithmic Bias from the Perspectives of Healthcare Professionals arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines algorithmic bias in machine learning and AI applications within healthcare information systems. Drawing on a survey and interviews with healthcare professionals in different job roles, it studies how bias, perceived fairness, and acceptance of ML outcomes are related. The authors find that opinions on bias causes, assessment criteria, fairness, and mitigation vary by role and algorithm characteristics. The paper concludes that further research is needed to ensure fairness and equality in healthcare.

entry.title: "It Would Make a Geordie Feel at Home": How Users Perceive and Adapt to Regional Accents in Voice AI
entry.summary: "It Would Make a Geordie Feel at Home": Regional Accent Perceptions and Speech Accommodation in Voice AI arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This study examines Newcastle English (Geordie) speakers' reactions to a simulated voice assistant speaking either Geordie or Standard Southern British English, and their own speech when voice technology fails to recognise them. The regional voice was linked to familiarity, warmth and local belonging, but also to concerns about professionalism and authority, while the standard voice seemed more neutral and credible. Participants often shifted toward a mainstream accent, enunciated more clearly or spoke more slowly after recognition failures.

entry.title: Are seismic foundation models more than advanced feature extractors?
entry.summary: Are Seismic Foundation Models More Than Glorified Feature Extractors? arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper examines foundation models for seismic waveforms, training nine designs on one Mamba encoder-decoder with a fixed corpus of 3M windows while varying the self-supervised objective, quantization bottleneck, and mixer. Frozen evaluation on three downstream tasks shows that changing the objective redistributes skill rather than raising it, and no checkpoint is best everywhere. The authors argue that the learning targets are defined over single fixed-length windows and miss the event-level occurrence process, so these models behave as feature extractors rather than foundation models.

entry.title: New multiple-descent effects caused by heterogeneous data
entry.summary: New Multiple Descent Phenomena Induced by Heterogeneous Data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how mixing datasets with different covariance structures can produce multiple-descent behavior in linear random-feature models. The authors derive exact asymptotic test-error expressions for each data source in the high-dimensional regime, showing that heterogeneity in covariance scale and spectrum introduces group-dependent interpolation thresholds. These effects appear even with noiseless labels and linear activations. The theory is validated on synthetic Gaussian mixtures and on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

entry.title: Keeping Safety Intact During Sequential Fine-Tuning: Replay Analysis
entry.summary: Preserving Safety During Sequential Fine-Tuning: A Factorial and Geometric Analysis of Replay arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how large language models lose safety alignment when fine-tuned in sequence and how to prevent it. It separates two strategies, supervised replay of refusal and compliance examples and logit distillation from the base model, and tests them on Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B.
