Supervised replay cuts attack success most but causes heavy over-refusal, while distillation largely prevents safety erosion at a much lower cost. Geometric analysis finds that preserving the base refusal direction is not a reliable indicator of behavioral safety.

entry.title: QMUL_AK's Arabic Function-Calling System for AISA-ArabicFC 2026 Using ALLaM with Schema Constraints
entry.summary: QMUL_AK at AISA-ArabicFC: Schema-Constrained Function Calling with ALLaM arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper describes the QMUL_AK team's submission to the AISA-ArabicFC 2026 shared task. The system fine-tunes the Arabic-English ALLaM-7B-Instruct model for function calling using low-rank adaptation (LoRA), combined with an Arabic schema-aware prompt, dialect and no-call resampling, a token-weighted training objective, and deterministic validation of generated calls. The authors report that function selection is nearly saturated, while argument extraction remains the main source of error.

entry.title: Generalizing Pretrained All-Atom Representations to Unified Binder Design
entry.summary: Towards Generalizing Pretrained All-Atom Representations to Unified Binder Design arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces PairFuse, a parameter-efficient method that fuses pretrained all-atom representations into an independently pretrained geometric latent diffusion model for unified binder design. It uses lightweight layerwise adapters to enrich molecular block features and to incorporate pairwise structural information into the denoiser. The authors report that across antibody, peptide, and small molecule binder-design benchmarks, PairFuse outperforms the pretrained diffusion model and existing representation-fusion baselines.

entry.title: Deep learning for screening non-transvenous defibrillators to reduce inappropriate shocks
entry.summary: Deep learning for non-transvenous ICD screening: tailored neural network architectures, extended experiments, and explainability arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies two non-transvenous implantable defibrillators, the Subcutaneous ICD and the Extravascular ICD, which avoid lead complications but can oversense heart signals and trigger inappropriate shocks. The authors present a 24-hour ambulatory screening framework and introduce AmpRatioNet, a 1D convolutional neural network that operates directly on ECG signals. Evaluated on 4,605 clinician-annotated 10-second segments from 89 patients, AmpRatioNet-SE outperforms the best existing approach on every metric.

entry.title: GAUSS: A Workload-Aware Simulator Predicting LLM Inference Latency and Capacity
entry.summary: GAUSS: A Workload-Aware Analytical and Monte-Carlo Simulator for LLM Inference Serving arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents GAUSS, a workload-aware analytical and Monte-Carlo simulator for LLM inference serving. It predicts the distributions of time-to-first-token and time-between-tokens, along with sustainable request rate, for a given workload, engine, and accelerator. GAUSS combines phase-specific latency models for prefill and decode with a Lindley-recurrence queueing model, using ensemble Monte-Carlo sampling to capture latency tails that trace-driven simulators under-sample. The authors show it supports operating-point selection, traffic segmentation, and shortest-remaining-processing-time scheduling analysis.

entry.title: Predicting sparse flow measurements with coarse-mesh graph neural networks
entry.summary: Predicting Sparse Observables in Parameterized Unsteady Flows Using Coarse-Mesh Graph Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes reduced-order models that use graph neural networks on coarse meshes to predict sparse probe locations and integrated quantities, avoiding full flow-field reconstruction. The models are applied to parameterized 2D and 3D confined cylinder flows and an unevenly heated cavity, and they generalize to unseen conditions. Coarse-mesh models match or outperform finer-mesh surrogates while reducing training time and memory.

entry.title: A hierarchical diffusion method for camera-controlled long video generation.
entry.summary: Hierarchical Diffusion for Camera-controlled Autoregressive Video Generation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses generating long videos from a single image under camera control. It proposes a lightweight framework combining autoregressive generation (WanAR) with hierarchical long-context denoising (FixAR), and reformulates video generation as a warping-and-inpainting problem to keep scene geometry consistent with input cameras. Experiments on RealEstate10k and DL3DV show the method outperforms prior approaches, producing results that are temporally stable and consistent with input camera trajectories.

entry.title: Separability Is Not Alignability: Representations for Spectrum-to-Molecule Retrieval
entry.summary: Separability Is Not Alignability: Representations for Spectrum-to-Molecule Retrieval arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies identifying small molecules from tandem mass spectra, a task limited by scarce paired data. It examines aligning separately pretrained spectrum and molecule encoders, testing this approach on MassSpecGym. The authors find that the objectives training spectrum encoders never account for molecular structure, so the distance metric needed for alignment is not guaranteed, and a candidate-based objective rewards a spectrum-independent prior. They conclude that simulated spectra outperform frozen geometry as a remedy for data scarcity.

entry.title: Solo movement style predicts group foraging, but whom to follow appears only in groups
entry.summary: Solitary movement style predicts collective foraging while whom to follow emerges only in company arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The study uses three public datasets of human collective foraging, with 621, 128 and 1,133 participants, to test whether solo behaviour predicts behaviour and performance in a group. Movement measured while alone predicted behaviour inside the group, and group performance was predicted from individually measured performance. Selective social learning, following those who succeeded or stopped, showed stable individual differences within groups but was not predicted from the same person's solo behaviour.

entry.title: Sometimes less is more: how MLPs and Transformers learn noisy k-parity features differently
entry.summary: Sometimes less is more: Investigating inductive biases of MLPs and Transformers on noisy k-parity features arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper compares how MLPs and Transformers learn from synthetic datasets built with noisy k-parity features, which allow precise control over each feature's predictivity and availability. Transformers handle noisy features more robustly but struggle with complex, low-availability ones, while MLPs show the opposite pattern and keep improving with more data. Under a fixed training budget, adding more unique training examples can slow Transformer optimisation enough to lower final accuracy, so a smaller dataset may perform better.

entry.title: FORGE: Online reference generation and full-body control for agile humanoid robot movement
entry.summary: FORGE: Feasible Online Reduced-Order Reference Generation and Whole-Body Execution for Agile Humanoid Locomotion arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a two-stage learning framework for agile, versatile humanoid locomotion. The first stage trains a command-conditioned whole-body reference generator using single rigid body dynamics and full humanoid kinematics. The second stage runs the frozen reduced-order policy online to produce references for training a whole-body tracking policy on the full-order model. Demonstrated on a Unitree G1 robot, the approach reaches longitudinal speeds from -2.0 to 2.8 m/s, lateral speeds up to ±1.0 m/s, and one-legged hopping.

entry.title: Merge and Branch: efficient tree-structured fine-tuning of LLMs for recommendation
entry.summary: Merge and Branch: Efficient Tree-Structured Supervised Fine-Tuning of LLMs for Recommendation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies LLM-based generative recommendation, where models read long interaction histories and generate short semantic identifiers. It proposes Merge and Branch (M&B), which compresses each historical item into a few learned tokens and uses this compressed history to predict multiple target identifiers arranged in a shallow, wide tree. The method introduces tree FlashAttention and a tree-structured key/value cache to share history computation. Experiments on public benchmarks report that M&B outperforms strong recommendation baselines while improving training and decoding efficiency.

entry.title: Applying PDE emulators to a multi-material, multi-physics simulation problem
entry.summary: Application of PDE emulators for a multi-material, multi-physics simulation problem arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper tests several computer vision-based machine learning architectures as surrogate models for a computational physics task involving multiple materials. It finds significant implementation difficulties in adapting some pre-trained models, including transformer-based ones. The authors argue that multi-physics, multi-material datasets call for learning methods suited to sparse and imbalanced data, adapted spatial encodings and physical consistency metrics, and lower-cost ways to generate training data.

entry.title: Meta-initialization to speed up deformable medical image registration with implicit neural representations
entry.summary: Meta-Initialization of Implicit Neural Representations to Accelerate Deformable Medical Image Registration arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses the slow per-image-pair adaptation of implicit neural representation (INR) methods for deformable medical image registration. It examines whether initializations learned from previously solved registration tasks, via Reptile meta-initialization and STRAINER transfer of a coordinate network's shared component, can accelerate early adaptation, using KAN-IDIR as the base model on OASIS-1. Both schemes achieve higher Dice and lower HD95 at early iterations than random initialization, with Reptile numerically better under a small iteration budget though pretraining budgets differ. The gap between the schemes narrows as iterations increase.

entry.title: Time-series world model conditioned on self-supervised latent actions
entry.summary: Self-Supervised Latent Action-Conditioned World Modeling for Time Series arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes ACTS-WM, a framework for time-series analysis that infers the information behind changes between observations as latent actions, without requiring explicit action annotations. It combines a JEPA-based encoder with an action-conditioned world model that predicts target time-series representations. The method is evaluated on 22 datasets from diverse domains across four tasks, including univariate and multivariate forecasting and classification. The authors report that it improves downstream performance over pretrained JEPA-based encoders by learning complementary representations.

entry.title: Statistical tests for position bias in LLM-based recommenders
entry.summary: Statistical Detection of Positional Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems: Methodologies and Empirical Evidence arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies positional bias in LLM-based recommender systems, where the recommended item depends on the order in which candidates appear in the prompt. The authors propose two statistical detection methods and run experiments on a real product catalog with 40,000 instances. Both methods find significant positional bias in all evaluated state-of-the-art models, which the authors describe as structural and model-dependent. They recommend routine auditing and controls such as order randomization.

entry.title: SAG-Sep: Sparse Augmented Graphs and Onion-Guided Search for Rounded Capacity Cut Separation
entry.summary: SAG-Sep: Sparse Augmented Graphs and Onion-Guided Search for Rounded Capacity Cut Separation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents SAG-Sep, a neural separator for rounded capacity cuts (RCCs) in capacitated vehicle-routing relaxations. It encodes a fractional LP solution as a sparse augmented graph and scores customer membership in one encoder pass. A training-free Onion-Sweep decoder then turns these scores into nested RCC candidates. On the N=1000 NeuralSEP benchmark, SAG-Sep with Onion-Sweep reduces the average root gap by 17.7% over the strongest NeuralSEP baseline, and the single-pass separator is roughly 30 times faster per iteration.

entry.title: Federated learning for semantic communication over shared wireless channels
entry.summary: Federated Learning for Semantic Communications over Multiple Access Channels arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a federated learning framework for semantic communication over a multiple access channel, where several distributed transmitters send learned semantic information to one receiver at the same time. Feature extraction, compression, wireless transmission, and semantic inference are optimized jointly. Evaluated on CIFAR-10 over fading channels, the approach keeps high inference accuracy and improves performance under severe data imbalance, while reducing training overhead.

entry.title: Knowledge Distillation Without Aligned Feature Spaces
entry.summary: You Don't Need Aligned Representations: Knowledge Distillation via Random Prototype Spaces arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes RPKD, a knowledge distillation method that compares teacher and student networks against a shared set of randomly initialized, frozen prototype vectors instead of aligning their feature spaces directly. It uses a logit branch and a feature branch, and reports that decoupling prototypes from the label space gives richer supervision when the number of classes is small. The authors report gains over OFA of up to +7.98% on CIFAR-100, +12.44% on ImageNet-100, and +1.28% on ImageNet-1K.

entry.title: Finite-step geometry of velocity fields that preserve marginals in generative flows
entry.summary: Finite-Step Geometry of Marginal-Preserving Velocity Fields in Generative Flows arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies why different velocity fields can produce the same continuous marginal evolution in generative flows yet behave differently after numerical discretization. Keeping the marginal path and numerical method fixed, the authors use projected modified equations to characterize the local integration error that changes the marginal law, and give sufficient conditions for higher marginal convergence order. For affine fixed-shape distributions they characterize exact finite-step reachability and derive spectral obstructions and sharp nearest-reachable Wasserstein errors, while for diffusion probability-flow ODEs they construct skew-score perturbations that preserve the marginal path under exact scores. Controlled Gaussian and mixture experiments recover the predicted order, reachability, and obstruction phenomena.

entry.title: SkillMem: Compact External Skill Memory for Efficient Latent Multi-Agent Reasoning
entry.summary: SkillMem: Compact External Skill Memory for Latent Multi-Agent Reasoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces SkillMem, which stores each reusable skill as a small external latent memory that is directly used during latent multi-agent reasoning. A role-conditioned cross-attention reader lets the same memory guide different agents according to their roles and hidden states. Tested on six benchmarks with Qwen3 models from 4B to 14B parameters, it gives strong gains for smaller models, needs 9.6 KB per skill, reduces storage over 38 times for a 100-skill library, and achieves up to a 4.23 times end-to-end inference speedup.

entry.title: Bi-Phase Training: a parameter-efficient method for learning language models from scratch
entry.summary: Bi-Phase Training: Learning Efficiently From Scratch arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Bi-Phase Training (BPT), a pre-training method that updates model weights using trainable diagonal matrices and low-rank adapters, periodically merging them into frozen base weights. Pre-training Qwen2.5 models (100M to 1.5B parameters) and OLMo-2-1B from scratch on FineWeb-Edu shows validation perplexity close to full-parameter baselines. At 1.5B scale, BPT uses 66% fewer trainable parameters, and it preserves much of the downstream task performance.

entry.title: NLP-based message prioritisation for opportunistic routing in disaster communication
entry.summary: NLP-based Message Prioritisation for Opportunistic Routing: A Case Study of Nepal Earthquake Emergency Communication arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This dissertation tests whether NLP-based semantic prioritisation can improve handling of urgent messages in opportunistic emergency networks, using the 2015 Nepal earthquake as a case study. TF-IDF with Logistic Regression and BERT classify social media messages into four routing priorities, applied within the ONE simulator. BERT yields higher priority accuracy and P1 recall, but network gains are inconsistent, with the clearest benefit appearing under buffer pressure.

entry.title: Study of whether large language models can work as numerical optimizers
entry.summary: Understanding Large Language Models as Numerical Optimizers arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper evaluates how well large language models solve numerical optimization problems, including convex optimization, fractional programming, and constrained projection. Their outputs are compared against deterministic reference solvers, separating solution quality from failures such as numerical errors, constraint violations, and format errors. The models often find near-optimal solutions, but reliability declines as problem dimension grows. Iterative refinement with feedback improves validity, and the authors propose hybrid approaches that pair LLM reasoning with deterministic numerical verification.

entry.title: Machine learning in the heliosphere: learned operators for modeling and forecasting Sun-to-ground space weather
entry.summary: Machine learning applications in the heliosphere arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This chapter examines space weather, the study of how Sun-driven processes affect the near-Earth environment. The authors treat the chain from the Sun to ground impacts as coupled systems, each described by a state vector and observables. Machine learning algorithms are framed as learned operators for inference, propagation, and emulation. The work argues this approach can improve understanding of the physical systems and speed up the development of operational space weather forecasting models.

entry.title: GARDEN: Autonomously designed reward functions that transfer across cooperative multi-agent scenarios
entry.summary: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026GARDEN is a method in which a large language model writes a single reward program for a family of related cooperative multi-agent learning scenarios. The program is then transferred unchanged to scenarios unseen during design. On unseen Overcooked and SMAX scenarios, task returns rose 58.2% and 52.5% over default rewards on two kitchen layouts, and mean win rate in two combat scenarios rose from 51.0% to 89.9%. These gains exceeded those from fixed diagnostic feedback and Eureka-inspired reward reflection under matched budgets.

entry.title: VerifiedLab: A multi-agent framework for turning verified research records into machine-usable knowledge
entry.summary: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces VerifiedLab, a multi-agent framework that converts research knowledge from human-oriented records into forms usable by AI systems. Its AI scientists with distinct roles verify records field by field, and a gate and critic check each claim against the reliability of its data before release. Experiments on perovskite solar cells show that the framework recovers known physical trends and anticipates devices reported a year later.

entry.title: FAD-KV: Adaptive Dictionary Caching to Speed Up Language Model Reasoning
entry.summary: FAD-KV: Adaptive Dictionary KV Caching for Efficient Reasoning Decoding arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes FAD-KV, a framework that compresses the key-value cache used by large language models during decoding. It represents each token's KV states as sparse combinations of learned dictionary atoms, using a one-shot Top-n screening step with lightweight coefficient refinement to limit computation. A fixed-size dictionary reuses inactive atoms so that it does not keep growing during generation. The authors report a strong quality-efficiency trade-off on reasoning and long-context benchmarks.

entry.title: SciGame: Letting AI Agents Play Scientific Discovery Games in Real and Altered Worlds
entry.summary: SciGame: Let Agents Play the Scientific Discovery Games in the Real and Counterfactual World arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces SciGame, a benchmark that converts scientific literature into structured cards and builds paired original and counterfactual environments with consistent units. It includes historical canonical laws and a temporal collection of papers published after model knowledge cutoffs, and tests agents in identification and open-ended discovery settings under prior-only, fixed, and adaptive protocols. Experiments on five frontier models find that familiar priors hurt performance when the governing relation is altered, adaptive experimentation helps strong models but harms weaker ones under limited budgets, and good explanations can hide quantitative errors. Recovering the exact symbolic form remains the main bottleneck.

entry.title: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Broader Vision-Forensics Foundation Model for Detecting Forgeries
entry.summary: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents Venus-DefakerOne2, a unified foundation model for detecting forgeries across digital manipulation and physical spoofing, in both images and videos. It is trained on tens of millions of open-source and in-house samples, using Tide-Style-Tuning, which alternates LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning, and Entropy-based Test Adaptation, which selects the prediction modality by analyzing prediction entropy. The authors report new state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks, outperforming specialized models and their predecessor, DefakerOne.

entry.title: What Actually Matters? A Paired Evaluation of Inference Settings for π0.5 on BEHAVIOR-1K
entry.summary: What Actually Matters? A Paired Evaluation of Inference Settings for π₀.5 on BEHAVIOR-1K arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper systematically compares previously proposed inference and data-collection strategies for household robot VLA models across all 100 BEHAVIOR-1K tasks. The evaluation uses a fine-tuned π0.5 model based on the 2025 BEHAVIOR Challenge winner, which scores 0.39 Q on the public test set. The results indicate that the proposed strategies do not transfer uniformly to new environments and tasks.

entry.title: Muon Optimizer Makes First MoE Layer's Load Harder to Balance
entry.summary: Muon Makes the First Mixture-of-Experts Layer Harder to Balance arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how the Muon optimizer affects the routing biases of mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models. In models with 55M and 108M active parameters, the span of the first MoE layer's biases roughly doubled under Muon. The rise traced to the first router's inputs sharing a direction, and subtracting the batch mean removed the overload. On the smaller model, halving Muon's learning rate removed most of the rise.

entry.title: Understanding Long Financial Texts with Semantically Enriched Tables Using Multimodal Learning
entry.summary: Grounding Long Financial Text with Semantically-Enriched Tables via Multimodal Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a multimodal Transformer framework for modeling long financial documents that combine structured tables with noisy textual disclosures. Each numerical variable is paired with a semantic embedding derived from its textual definition, and cross-attention integrates the tables with long-form text such as MD&A sections. Experiments on a large-scale dataset of financial statements and MD&A disclosures show that numerical features remain the dominant predictive signal, while cross-attention yields consistent gains over simple concatenation.

entry.title: Segmental evaluation of accent in speech generation, aligned with listener perception
entry.summary: Beyond Utterance-Level Speaker Similarity: Perception-Aligned Segmental Evaluation of Accent in Speech Generation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper argues that utterance-level similarity ratings cannot show where perceived accent differences occur in generated speech. It proposes a segmental protocol that combines speaker and accent similarity ratings with subword annotations of accent differences from listeners in target accent regions. Forty-seven retained listeners evaluated 200 content-matched reference–candidate pairs covering four Scottish and Australian voices, two zero-shot TTS systems, and an articulation-based voice conversion system. Speaker and accent ratings were strongly associated (ρ = 0.71), while seven objective distance measures showed weak correspondence with subword selections, reaching at most ρ = 0.22.

entry.title: Generative Modeling for Fusion: A Large-Scale Stellarator Fast-Ion Simulation Benchmark
entry.summary: Generative modeling for fusion: a large-scale benchmark of stellarator fast-ion simulations arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces BoSS, a dataset pairing stellarator designs with guiding center simulation results and particle trajectories for 180,000 magnetohydrodynamic equilibria. It formulates two machine learning tasks: generative modeling of stellarators with good particle confinement, and surrogate modeling of heat deposition patterns and particle trajectories. The authors report that their baselines generate diverse, performant stellarators and useful surrogate predictions, and they identify long-horizon trajectory forecasting and out-of-distribution generation as directions for future work.

entry.title: TERRA: Edge AI for regional fire detection that reports without device identity
entry.summary: TERRA: Task-Oriented Edge AI for Regional Fire Detection with Identity-Free Reporting arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents TERRA, an edge-AI framework for distributed fire monitoring in which devices send task-relevant local inference results tagged by region rather than by device identity, and a receiver aggregates the regional evidence in a permutation-invariant way. It evaluates two reporting modes, TERRA-Score and TERRA-Feature, using 15 sensing modalities from the EN54 indoor fire-alarm dataset. With nine reports and perfect message recovery, TERRA-Feature reaches mean AUPRC 0.990 with a 24-bit payload, and TERRA-Score reaches 0.987 with only 6 bits, both with an MDR of 1.81% at FAR at most 1%.

entry.title: Beyond Low-Pass Dynamics: Frequency-Selective Spiking Reservoirs with Resonant Neurons
entry.summary: Beyond Low-Pass Dynamics: Frequency-Selective Spiking Reservoirs with Resonant Neurons arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces HRF-Res, a liquid state machine that replaces the usual Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neurons with a heterogeneous population of Harmonic Resonate-and-Fire neurons, letting the reservoir respond to frequency-specific temporal patterns. Across ten benchmarks covering time series, sequential images, audio spike trains, and neuromorphic vision, it reports state-of-the-art accuracy among spiking reservoir methods. The authors state that this is achieved while preserving the energy efficiency of spiking computation.

entry.title: FilingLoop: Testing and Improving AI Agents That Review and Revise Company Disclosure Filings
entry.summary: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces FilingLoop, an interactive benchmark and self-evolving agent framework for reviewing and revising corporate disclosure filings. It is built from historical U.S. SEC correspondence, reconstructing 380 mostly IPO review tasks from 96 companies, scored against 6,099 requirements. The framework learns procedural guidance across cases without updating model weights, raising requirement fulfillment from 24.28% to 27.96% on the evaluated stream.

entry.title: "Think Twice": A Report on Two Language Models Built From Scratch
entry.summary: Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This report presents Metis-1.6, two language models trained from scratch by one researcher: Praxis (2.94B parameters) and Logos (10.23B parameters). Both process each token twice through a hybrid Mamba-2 and attention mixture-of-experts stack, and were trained on 1.02T tokens. Across 40 post-trained benchmarks, Logos averages 52.93, performing strongly in mathematics but weakly in code, instruction following and long context. The report also documents training mistakes and their fixes.

entry.title: SAC-GCL: Graph contrastive learning that uses structure-aware compression instead of random perturbations to create graph views
entry.summary: SAC-GCL: Structure-Aware Compression for Graph Contrastive Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes SAC-GCL, a framework for graph contrastive learning that replaces random augmentations such as edge perturbation and node masking with structural decomposition. It extracts cohesive subgraphs and condenses them into supernodes, producing coarsened graph views that preserve local density and higher-level structure. Multiple cohesive subgraph models yield complementary views, which a hierarchical view encoder processes. Experiments on six benchmark datasets show more robust and discriminative representations for graph classification.

entry.title: Role of Socio-Demographics and Reasoning in Pluralistic Offensiveness Modeling
entry.summary: The Anatomy of Socio-Demographics in Pluralistic Offensiveness Modeling: When and Where It Helps, and the Role of Reasoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines when and where annotators' socio-demographic information helps models predict offensiveness judgments, and whether explicit reasoning improves its use. Experiments on three multi-annotator datasets with prompted and trained LLMs show that demographic gains are small and inconsistent for individual predictions but clearer at group and population levels. Reasoning that decomposes judgments into a baseline and a demographic-specific deviation yields more accurate estimates than direct demographic conditioning.

entry.title: When More Planning Hurts: Learned Planners for World Models
entry.summary: When More Planning Hurts: Learned Planners for World Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies planning for robots using learned world models, comparing several planners on the PushT task. The proposed fixed action updater has 1,505 parameters and solves 8 of 16 reserved scenes. Experiments with additional update budgets found that extra updates rescued no failing tasks and instead caused some previously successful tasks to fail.

entry.title: FYC: FPR-Disparity Weight Perturbation and Youden Calibration for Fair Deepfake Detection
entry.summary: FYC: FPR-Disparity Weight Perturbation and Youden Calibration for Fair Deepfake Detection arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses demographic disparities in deepfake detectors, where false-positive rates differ notably across gender and skin-tone groups. It proposes FYC, a two-stage post-hoc method that perturbs detector weights under an FPR-disparity criterion and then calibrates a separate decision threshold per group, without architectural changes or full retraining. On AI-Face v2 across six intersectional gender by skin-tone groups, FYC outperforms the compared detectors on 18 of 21 fairness and utility metrics.

entry.title: Fair Deepfake Detection via Intersectional Invariant Learning
entry.summary: Intersectional Invariant Learning for Fair Deepfake Detection arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Deepfake detectors often perform unevenly across demographic groups, with some groups facing much higher false-positive rates. This paper proposes Intersectional Invariant Learning (IIL), which improves feature learning rather than only adjusting model outputs, and covers six gender by skin-tone intersectional groups. Evaluated on a benchmark of over one million images against 10 baseline detectors using 21 metrics, IIL reports high AUC, false-positive rates under 2.5%, and the lowest intersectional fairness disparity among compared methods.

entry.title: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data
entry.summary: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents nn-EQL, a framework that generates candidate equations by iteratively training, pruning, and retraining a neural network with user-specified activation functions. Candidates are ranked by a minimum description length-inspired score balancing error and sparsity. The method is demonstrated on standard AI-Feynman benchmarks and on high-dimensional materials datasets, including finite-element simulations of heterogeneous materials and high-throughput thin-film deposition data.

entry.title: Verification Learning Theory: A model of how AI-assisted checking affects retained judgment skills
entry.summary: Verification Learning Theory: A Process Model of Checking and Retention in AI-Assisted Judgment arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes Verification Learning Theory (VLT), a process model describing how checking evidence during AI-assisted claim evaluation affects later independent judgment. The model links perceived assistant reliability to evidence checking and the history of checks to retained rule use. Simulations examine the consequences and parameter dependence of its assumptions, and the paper identifies where its predictions diverge from alternative accounts and specifies experiments to test the proposed mechanism.

entry.title: PairCLIP-SWA: A single-model deepfake image detector using similarity-guided balancing and weight averaging
entry.summary: PairCLIP-SWA: Similarity-Guided Balancing and Stochastic Weight Averaging for Generalized Deepfake Image Detection with OpenCLIP arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper presents PairCLIP-SWA, a deepfake image detector built on a single OpenCLIP ViT-L/14 visual backbone, trained on a class-balanced set created by CLIP-similarity-guided one-to-one subsampling. Its fine-tuning trajectory is averaged in weight space. On the IEEE SP Cup 2025 (DF-Wild-Cup) benchmark, the weight-averaged model reaches 97.04% accuracy, 98.64% AU-ROC and a 4.07% equal error rate. The authors show that checkpoints selected by validation accuracy can be unstable and recommend per-class selection criteria measured on a split separate from early stopping.

entry.title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning models how agreement design affects global climate cooperation
entry.summary: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Global Climate Policy Cooperation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper extends an existing multi-agent reinforcement learning climate framework with a multi-stage negotiation mechanism where agents propose, accept or reject agreements, and face penalties for non-compliance. In an idealized setting with four homogeneous agents, non-binding agreements do little to stop free-riding, while moderate penalties improve cooperation and reduce warming. However, excessively strong penalties discourage ambitious commitments. The authors present the framework as a methodological tool for testing agreement design rather than a predictive model of real negotiations.

entry.title: What Food Similarity Means: Visual Representations and Retrieval in Indian Cuisine
entry.summary: What Constitutes Food Similarity? Visual Representations and Retrieval in Indian Cuisine arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines food similarity beyond simple identity matching, comparing how seven pretrained visual models group Indian dishes into neighborhoods in image retrieval. The neighborhoods differ substantially across representations, including some similarities crossing culinary-family boundaries. At the dish level, the models share some visual structure, but it corresponds only weakly to recipe-derived similarity, suggesting food similarity depends on representation and abstraction level.

entry.title: Echo: scaling visual reinforcement learning with off-policy experience
entry.summary: Echo: Scaling Visual Reinforcement Learning with Off-policy Experience arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Echo, a single-stage off-policy reinforcement learning framework that collects experience without proportionally increasing visual rendering and inference costs. Through inverse distillation, a state-based auxiliary policy imitates the evolving visual policy and gathers inexpensive, unrendered experience used for off-policy value learning. Implemented with FastTD3 and tested in Genesis on three visual locomotion tasks and two dexterous hand manipulation tasks, Echo reduces time to reference returns by about 60% on average for the locomotion tasks and 56% for the hand tasks, relative to the compared method. It also improves peak mean returns by 62% and 12% respectively.

entry.title: Effects of Deep Learning Architecture and Pretraining on Automated Vocal Fold Segmentation in High-Speed Phonation Images
entry.summary: Effects of Deep Learning Architecture and Pretraining on Automated Vocal Fold Segmentation in Ex Vivo High-Speed Phonation Images arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This study compares four deep learning architectures (UNet, UNet++, TransUNet, Swin-UNet) for automatically segmenting vocal folds in high-speed images from ex vivo canine larynx phonation experiments. It uses 16,344 expert-annotated images from 227 trials. Mean Dice scores were similar across models, with differences mainly in boundary accuracy. ImageNet pretraining significantly improved boundary metrics for TransUNet and Swin-UNet, and without pretraining TransUNet outperformed the two CNN-based models on boundary fidelity.

entry.title: Seq@K: Testing How Language Models Improve from Feedback
entry.summary: Seq@K: Evaluating Language Models Under Sequential Feedback arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Seq@K, an evaluation protocol that checks whether a language model can solve a problem within K sequential attempts, receiving feedback after each failure. It isolates the ability to refine answers based on feedback, unlike benchmarks focused on long-horizon planning. Tested on 7 benchmarks and 16 frontier models, Seq@K yields model rankings and efficiency trade-offs that differ from Pass@K.

entry.title: Testing whether AI agents can accurately rebuild sequencing protocols
entry.summary: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces LibStructBench, a document-based benchmark that tests whether AI agents can reconstruct sequencing-library structures and molecular workflows from sequencing protocols. The experiments show that frontier agents often produce roughly correct reconstructions but are unreliable at exact reconstruction, especially for molecular-state representation and workflow connectivity. Switching the underlying language model caused larger average performance differences than switching agent harnesses, and only the molecular-state reconstruction difference was statistically significant.

entry.title: Detecting hidden AI agent collusion via partner-outsider positive listening
entry.summary: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes a behavioural test for AI agents that share a secret code. A partner using the code reacts to the exact wording of a message, while an uninvolved outsider does not. The method, Partner–Outsider Positive Listening (PoPLi), measures the difference between the two agents' action changes when messages are reworded with the same meaning, computed by replaying logged prompts. In a simulated market, PoPLi was high when a code was present and near zero without it, while message-only monitors failed to distinguish the conditions.

entry.title: Learning convex potentials to compute optimal transport between medical images
entry.summary: Convex Potential Learning for Optimal Transport Between Medical Images arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes a method that estimates optimal transport maps between medical images by parameterizing a convex potential function. The resulting map is curl-free by construction, consistent with Brenier's theorem. The method is evaluated on 2D and 3D medical imaging datasets, and the authors report lower transport estimation errors and higher-quality image reconstructions than existing approaches.

entry.title: Where the Error Lives: Spectral Representations of Learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians
entry.summary: Where the Error Lives: Spectral Representations of Learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies machine-learned models that predict Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian matrices to replace costly self-consistent-field calculations in density functional theory. It shows that matching matrix entries does not ensure accurate eigenvalues or eigenvectors, and that two existing physics-informed losses each capture only part of the error. The authors propose the cumulative local density of states as a complete training signal and report that fine-tuning on QH9, called FermiScope, reduces the HOMO-LUMO gap error without increasing element-wise error.

entry.title: Better scaling for large language models when training data is limited
entry.summary: Improving Data-Constrained Scaling with Hyperparameter Transfer and Ensembling arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to train large language models when both compute and high-quality data are limited. The authors fit power laws that specify how key hyperparameters should transfer across model sizes and epochs, and scaling laws that specify how to allocate compute through ensembling. On 100M tokens from FineWeb, their recipe lowers validation loss by over 0.15 nats compared with prior recipes, a 14% perplexity decrease, and improves monotonically with compute via ensembling.

entry.title: Depth Through Recurrence: Compact Speech Recognition for Edge Devices
entry.summary: Depth through Recurrence: Towards Ultra-Efficient On-Device ASR arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes a block-recurrent speech recognition architecture that replaces many independent layers with a few recurrent blocks of weight-shared layers, keeping effective depth while shrinking model size. Using representation-guided grouping and knowledge distillation, a model with only two shared blocks reportedly reaches 97.4% of large models' accuracy on average across Open ASR Leaderboard benchmarks. The compact design also supports lightweight on-device personalization via MoE-LoRA adaptation and lower memory and energy use.

entry.title: DeFT-RAG: Breaking Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
entry.summary: DeFT-RAG: Incrementally Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes DeFT-RAG, a retrieval-augmented generation framework for multi-hop questions that require chaining facts across several documents. It has the language model generate one self-contained sub-question at a time, while rule-based updates and a lightweight decision model handle the remaining tasks, and it caches question-answer pairs for reuse. On MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA and HotpotQA, it achieves the best accuracy among thirteen baselines and uses fewer input tokens than other iterative methods. With a cache shared across 1,000 MuSiQue questions, 23.1% of sub-questions were answered from the cache, reducing LLM calls by 12.9% without lowering accuracy.

entry.title: Learning Without Clocks: Neural Networks Invariant to How Event Streams Are Split
entry.summary: Learning Without Clocks: Partition-Invariant Neural Network arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Event sensors output asynchronous events, but most learning systems first group them into frames, making results depend on how the stream is sliced. The paper studies networks that update their state exactly at each event and evolve in closed form between events, so their output does not depend on this slicing. It proves conditions for order-independence of simultaneous events and continuity in timestamps, and introduces a learnable Clock-Free Event (CFE) layer. In preliminary development-set experiments, the proposed state outperforms an otherwise identical additive state on several event datasets.

entry.title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Subgroups
entry.summary: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper empirically audits the fairness of classical and quantum classifiers for medical imaging, assuming quantum machine learning is not inherently fair. It compares SVM, MLP, QSVM and QCNN on dermatological lesions (DDI, with Fitzpatrick skin type as the sensitive attribute) and chest X-rays (CheXpert-derived, with age group as the attribute), testing several mitigation methods. The quantum models can be competitive overall yet still show subgroup disparities, and fairness effects depend on the model and dataset. All quantum models run in classical simulation, and the authors claim no quantum advantage.

entry.title: GOFish: Full-field-of-view Gaussian splatting that builds scene meshes from fisheye images
entry.summary: GOFish: Full Field-of-View Gaussian Splatting and Mesh Extraction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Fisheye lenses give robots, self-driving cars, and 360° cameras a wide view, but earlier Gaussian splatting methods rendered only up to 180° and produced no meshes. GOFish is the first Gaussian splatting surface reconstruction method that trains directly on fisheye images, renders beyond 180°, and extracts an aligned mesh from the same scene. It improves PSNR over the best prior method by 2.28 dB on FIORD (200°) and 1.97 dB on FullCircle (205°), and achieves the highest mesh F-score on FIORD and the main ScanNet++ set.

entry.title: What an Ontology Catches: Curated, LLM-Generated, and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents
entry.summary: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies ontology-based checkers that judge answers from LLM agents querying Web knowledge graphs. It compares curated, LLM-generated, and data-derived ontologies, used as prompt context or as checkers, to see which errors each catches and which correct answers each wrongly flags. On UniProt, the curated ontology flags more correct answers than either alternative. On real agent answers, its flags are only marginally more precise than random flags.

entry.title: Spokes, Not a Ring: Revisiting How Language Models Represent Weekdays
entry.summary: Spokes, not a Ring: Revisiting the Weekday Manifold in Language Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines how large language models represent weekdays as a circular geometric structure, called a manifold. The authors test whether moving continuously along this manifold corresponds to a smooth change in the represented concept. They find that weekday representations behave more like seven discrete states arranged in a circle than a continuous ring. The intermediate space between these states does not appear to encode time of day, uncertainty, or natural text.

entry.title: Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform: adaptive window length for time-frequency analysis
entry.summary: Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform: Data-Adaptive Window-Length Selection for Time-Frequency Analysis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The short-time Fourier transform analyzes local frequency content with a sliding window, but short windows favor time resolution while long windows favor frequency resolution. This paper proposes the Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform (U-STFT), which treats window duration as a data-adaptive state chosen frame by frame, scoring candidate windows with normalized order-three Rényi entropy and aggregating them through a window-length trellis. The authors give a cumulative regret bound and show on synthetic and marine bioacoustic signals adaptive resolution tracking, improved spectral concentration, and exact time-domain invertibility.

entry.title: Where sycophancy appears across training stages of open language models
entry.summary: Locating Sycophancy Across Training Stages in Open Language Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies sycophancy, where language models change correct answers after a user suggests a wrong one. The authors measured 13 open checkpoints from 5 model lineages at every available training stage, from base model to release. They find two sycophancy behaviors with different origins: deference to claims in the prompt is already present in base models, while conversational capitulation is largely absent from base models and appears in all post-trained checkpoints.

entry.title: Sparse tensor networks for estimating individual tree diameter in mixed forests
entry.summary: Sparse tensor networks for individual tree diameter estimation in mixed forests arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to automatically estimate individual tree diameter at breast height (DBH) from UAV laser scanning point clouds. The authors introduce TreeNext, a lightweight deep learning architecture that estimates tree parameters directly from voxelized LiDAR data, and build a full pipeline from instance segmentation to DBH regression on four mixed temperate forest plots in Germany. TreeNext reaches an R² of 0.8355 on automatically segmented trees and 0.9380 on ground truth segments, outperforming Random Forest and XGBoost. The study finds that segmentation quality is the dominant error source in the automated pipeline.

entry.title: Selective and Hybrid-State Communication for Latent Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary: Selective and Hybrid-State Communication for Latent Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper tackles the communication cost of large language model multi-agent systems, which exchange internal model states instead of repeated natural language. It proposes two complementary methods: SelectKV, which selectively communicates KV states while protecting inherited context, and HyLaMAS, which extends latent collaboration to hybrid linear-attention models by sharing both KV caches and recurrent states. According to the abstract, SelectKV cuts communicated KV positions and logical KV payload by 9.7-9.9% across six benchmarks, with accuracy largely preserved. HyLaMAS reduces decoded output tokens by 53-80% and achieves 1.16-2.78x speedups over text-based communication on Qwen3.5 models.

entry.title: MDraft: Multi-Draft On-Policy Distillation for Training Parallel Diffusion Drafters
entry.summary: Multi-Draft On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Drafters arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to train one-step diffusion drafters that propose several tokens in parallel for speculative decoding, a technique that speeds up language model inference. The authors show that when verifier feedback is used separately for each sampled prefix, the targets conflict and can suppress tokens that are plausible under some prefixes. They introduce MDraft, which samples several draft blocks from the same context and aggregates the verifier's full-vocabulary conditionals across their prefixes. Experiments on mathematical, coding, and conversational tasks show longer accepted drafts than prior distillation methods, and the method changes only training, keeping the architecture and inference procedure unchanged.

entry.title: EUReCA: A Unified Deep Learning Method for Flexible Cone-Beam CT Reconstruction
entry.summary: EUReCA: End-to-End Unified CBCT Reconstruction Across Clinical Acquisitions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper presents EUReCA, a geometry-aware feed-forward model that reconstructs cone-beam CT images from 8 to 100 projections using a single set of weights, for clinical linear accelerator scans. It combines learned projection features with an FDK reconstruction and refines the volume with a global 3D transformer. On simulated data it reached 29.9 to 33.2 dB PSNR with 10 to 100 views, outperforming feed-forward baselines and running much faster than iterative methods. On 15 measured patient scans compared against vendor reconstructions, it achieved the best performance at every tested view count.

entry.title: OpenFrontiers: Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Rediscovering Science
entry.summary: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces OpenFrontiers, a resource combining a corpus of 12,151 open research problems with a benchmark of 200 mathematics problems, 110 resolved in 2026 and 90 still open. The benchmark problems come with Lean 4 formal statements and are graded with formal proofs. Seven LLM agents were evaluated on the HQ-50 subset, and closed-book rediscovery succeeded on at most 7 of 40 resolved problems, while live-web success mostly reflected retrieval of published solutions.

entry.title: Anisotropic trust region warping to improve Prior-Data Fitted Networks in Bayesian optimisation
entry.summary: Anisotropic Trust Region Warping for Prior-Data Fitted Networks in Bayesian Optimisation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs), which replace refitting Gaussian Process surrogates in Bayesian optimisation with a single forward pass. The authors show that when the objective's lengthscale grows beyond the mode of the PFN's meta-training prior, the PFN's predictive log-likelihood falls behind a refitted GP, and this gap affects optimisation performance. They propose Anisotropic Trust Region (ATR) warping, which estimates per-dimension lengthscales by kernel target alignment and applies an affine rescaling of the input space without retraining the network. On functions drawn from a Matérn-3/2 kernel, ATR warping improves the PFN's optimisation performance at both ends of the lengthscale range.

entry.title: Selective transfer learning to forecast groundwater level anomalies, weighing accuracy against risk
entry.summary: Selective Transfer Learning for Groundwater Level Anomaly Forecasting: Accuracy-Risk Trade-offs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies context-aware selective transfer learning for forecasting groundwater anomalies across many wells in the Netherlands. Pretraining on source-domain data raises average accuracy but harms a substantial share of heterogeneous wells. The proposed CASL method learns, on calibration data, a constrained contextual blend of a no-transfer model and a fixed-transfer model, while Global Convex Neither method dominates; the results show an accuracy-risk trade-off on a fixed split rather than validity for rolling deployment.

entry.title: ThinkJev: Calibrated Choice-Making by Language Models with Adaptive Thinking
entry.summary: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents ThinkJev, a framework for language models that must choose among a fixed set of options. It builds a fast system that reads option probabilities directly and a slow system that reads them after the model thinks on the same cached prompt. At a 5% target error rate, Qwen3.5-27B answers 24.5% of 8359 test decisions directly with a realized error of 3.9%. For the remaining decisions, stopping thoughts once confident reaches 81.6% accuracy, compared with 82.7% for always thinking, using 72% of the thought tokens.

entry.title: Amortized localized posterior inference for calibrating models, applied to an ocean turbulence closure
entry.summary: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper proposes a localized posterior calibration method that weights observation likelihoods by their proximity to a target context, approximating the family of posteriors with a conditional normalizing flow via amortized variational inference. Integrating these posteriors under a context measure yields a marginalized parameter distribution. In a Branin-Hoo twin experiment, localization reduced aggregate predictive errors relative to the global posterior. Applied to the k-ε turbulence closure in a single-column ocean model with atmospheric forcing as context, localized calibration reduced temperature and zonal-velocity errors compared with deterministic and global-posterior calibration.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity Search: Knowledge Graph Metadata for Enterprise RAG
entry.summary: Beyond Similarity Search: Knowledge Graph Metadata Enrichment for Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether storing metadata and frequently changing information in a knowledge graph improves enterprise retrieval-augmented generation over embedding-based similarity search. The authors built a snapshot of SEC EDGAR filings for one quarter and compared text-to-SQL, dense-vector RAG, and a two-stage GraphRAG design. GraphRAG answered 16 of 20 questions correctly on all three attempts, versus 10 for text-to-SQL and 3 for vector RAG, though it performed worse on structured aggregation queries.

entry.title: Predicate Neuron: Differentiable Logic Reasoning Module for Neural Networks
entry.summary: Predicate Neuron: Differentiable Quantization of Predicate Relations in Gradient-based Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces the Native Predicate Neuron, a differentiable module that adds symbolic logic reasoning to standard neural networks via first-order logic quantization. It learns to switch between logical operations using a single trainable parameter, executing hard logic during training while remaining differentiable for backpropagation. Tested on fully-connected, convolutional, recurrent, and Transformer models with MNIST and Wikitext, it generally speeds convergence, improves accuracy, and lowers loss, especially for monotonic reasoning and discontinuous functions.

entry.title: Threshold compatibility and support-selection checks in neural PDE discovery
entry.summary: Threshold Compatibility and Support-Selection Diagnostics in Neural Discovery of Partial Differential Equations arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper studies whether accurate regression in neural PDE discovery guarantees the correct equation after support selection. For a median/sample-standard-deviation threshold, it derives an exact two-signal retention boundary and a complete-vector perturbation bound. Experiments show an exact advection-diffusion library loses the diffusion term even when coefficients are recovered to numerical precision.

entry.title: LRMoE: Memory-Aware Training System for Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Models
entry.summary: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Sparse Mixture-of-Experts models scale capacity but suffer computation and communication bottlenecks from uneven routing, and existing expert replication competes with token buffers for limited GPU memory. LRMoE is a memory-aware MoE training system that recalibrates backward demand by selecting token-expert pairs within retention quotas, distributes them with capacity-aware routing, and compacts the workload to reduce backward traffic and buffer needs. On Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B, it cuts cumulative MoE-layer training time to fixed-loss targets by 21.2 to 44.8 percent relative to SYMI.

entry.title: GraphBARC: Smart Multi-Step Sampling for Building Radio Signal Maps
entry.summary: Learning Graph Beliefs for Active Radio Mapping With Decision-Certified Multi-Step Sensing arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces GraphBARC, a framework that builds radio maps by choosing where to take signal measurements. A graph network learns spatial relationships among measurement locations to form a joint belief over the full map. The method plans multi-step measurement routes by evaluating map-wide Bayes risk reduction and prunes unpromising routes using error-aware bounds. Experiments report over 16% lower mean RMSE than the evaluated baselines and 56% less core planning time than an unpruned fixed-accuracy implementation.

entry.title: Machine learning and deep learning for detecting heart attacks from ECG signals
entry.summary: Towards Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis: An Investigation into Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms using ECG Data arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper proposes Visionary V2, a multi-step adaptive filtering method for normalizing ECG signals, and uses it to study machine and deep learning for myocardial infarction detection on the PTB Diagnostic ECG Database. A bagged decision tree ensemble using statistical features such as R-R intervals reaches 96.6% accuracy, compared with 87.7% when signals are processed with BioSPPy. Image models built from the filtered signals achieve an F1 score of about 98.7% for a custom CNN, and explainability methods (LIME, Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients) are used to check that the models focus on the ECG waveform.

entry.title: Search-guided selection of reasoning traces for Verilog code generation
entry.summary: Search-Guided Reasoning Trace Curation for Verilog Generation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents MCTS-SFT, a framework that uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to select reasoning traces for fine-tuning Verilog generation models, propagating functional feedback from complete RTL rollouts to earlier design decisions. It introduces Plan-MCTS, which searches over structured hardware-design plans covering interfaces, timing, state, behavior, and update rules. The authors report that Plan-MCTS yields 84.2% correct traces and that retaining the searched plan during fine-tuning raises pass@10 from 52.56% to 57.7%.

entry.title: Balancing travel efficiency and pollution exposure at mega events with multi-agent routing
entry.summary: Balancing Mobility Efficiency and Environmental Exposure During Mega Events: A Multi-agent Routing Framework arXiv · Oct 26, 2026This paper proposes a multi-agent routing framework for short-term high-demand travel during mega events, accounting for travelers' exposure to traffic-related pollution. The framework integrates road-network conditions, event-induced demand, background traffic, and environmental data in one simulation environment. Under high demand, the SARSA-based framework reduces vehicle travel time by 34.59% and cumulative environmental exposure by 58.65%, while micro-mobility travel time stays nearly unchanged.

entry.title: DuQUAD: A Dual-View Framework for Multi-Document Question Answering with Quality-Aware Evidence Filtering
entry.summary: DuQUAD: A Dual-View Framework with Quality-Aware Evidence Pruning for Multi-Document Question Answering arXiv · Oct 25, 2026Retrieval-augmented language models often overlook evidence placed in the middle of long multi-document contexts, a problem known as Lost in the Middle. The paper proposes DuQUAD, which pairs a Local Agent guided by a Structural Fusion Score with a Global Agent that reasons over the full document set. It also scores candidate evidence for quality and refines it at the sentence level to reduce noise. The authors report higher accuracy and gold evidence recall than strong baselines, with lower computational cost than existing multi-agent frameworks.

entry.title: Coordination Costs and Model Heterogeneity in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines: Break-Even Conditions
entry.summary: The Coordination Tax and the Heterogeneity Dividend: Break-Even Conditions for Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines arXiv · Oct 25, 2026The paper gives a closed-form model that weighs the coordination cost of multi-agent LLM pipelines (task decomposition and per-handoff protocol overhead) against the benefit of routing work to a cheaper model, with a break-even threshold and a feasibility bound. Measured on 135 HumanEval and ClassEval tasks across 2430 runs, decomposition did not pay off: a planner-coder-reviewer pipeline cost 3.22 times a single strong-model call and solved no more tasks. The authors conclude that choosing a model per task performs better than splitting work across roles.

entry.title: Bouba Beats Kiki: Regularities in LLMs' Subjective Preferences
entry.summary: Bouba Beats Kiki, and Other Regularities in the Subjective Preferences of LLMs arXiv · Oct 21, 2026This paper examines how large language models choose among multiple viable responses when no answer is clearly correct. The authors study short-form content, namely numbers, baby names, and fictional cities, and identify 29 syntactic and semantic aspects of these items. They report that models show strong, reproducible preferences for some aspects, and that the way a preference is requested can change which aspects influence the selection.

entry.title: Two-Colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on Rectangles: Forbidden-Pattern Characterization, Polynomial Algorithm, and Lean Verification
entry.summary: Two-Colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on Rectangles: A Forbidden-Pattern Characterization, a Constructive Polynomial-Time Algorithm, and a Lean Verification arXiv · Oct 20, 2026The paper studies the zig-zag numberlink problem on rectangular grids with two endpoint pairs, where the disjoint paths must together visit every cell. For rectangles with both sides at least 11, it gives a finite catalogue of forbidden patterns whose absence is necessary and sufficient for solvability, together with a constructive polynomial-time algorithm. Instances with a side at most 10 are decided by frontier dynamic programming, and both directions of the characterization and the dynamic programming are verified in Lean 4.

entry.title: Cassette-Editor: A Video Editing Agent That Works Like a Human Editor
entry.summary: Cassette-Editor: A Video Editing Agent That Edits the Way You Do arXiv · Oct 19, 2026The paper presents Cassette-Editor, a video editing agent with just two tools, one to read the project and one to write to it. Every write goes through the same executor, rules, and commit service as manual edits, either committing atomically or being rejected with located diagnostics and repair options. In a controlled experiment, the model corrected nearly all of 277 of its own committed edits after they were damaged. Locating each problem cut the input tokens needed for a correction to less than half.

entry.title: Generative AI as an invisible hand shaping group opinions in simulated discussions
entry.summary: GenAI as an 'Invisible Hand' in Opinion Dynamics: Evidence from a Group-Level Simulation Study arXiv · Oct 18, 2026This paper examines whether generative AI can gradually shape collective beliefs and norms through repeated use. Using a simulation of 50,000 group discussions across 50 controversial statements, three LLMs and different social configurations, the authors compare AI influence in homogeneous and heterogeneous groups. They find that profile-specific personalization increases LLM influence when models take a non-neutral stance, and that neutral LLMs have a stronger effect in homogeneous groups.

entry.title: One Threshold, Unequal Coverage: Language Gaps in Automated AI Decisions and Fixes
entry.summary: One Confidence Threshold, Unequal Coverage: Language Gaps in Typed Decision Interfaces and How Translating Inputs Reduces Them arXiv · Oct 18, 2026This paper examines whether one confidence threshold treats all languages equally in typed decision interfaces that return option probabilities for fixed multiple-choice questions. Three vendors' interfaces were tested on 1,000 MASSIVE items across 51 languages at a 0.9 threshold. English cleared the threshold 8.6 to 11.7 percentage points more often on average, and translating inputs into English nearly closes the gap at that threshold. The authors recommend reporting per-language coverage at the operating threshold.

entry.title: Rethinking Social Simulation in Open-Population Systems: From Persistent Agents to Communication Processes
entry.summary: Rethinking Social Simulation in Open-Population Systems: From Persistent Agents to Communication Processes arXiv · Oct 17, 2026This paper argues that large-scale social networks are open-population systems where users enter and leave, and only a sparse subset is observable through communication. Instead of simulating persistent individual state trajectories, the authors model the observable evolution of social communication, including who participates, what they say, and how this shapes later system dynamics. Across five Qwen backbones, the framework reduces average KL divergence by 71.2% over Direct LLM and 35.0% over MF-LLM.

entry.title: Where Planning Changes Outcomes in Orbital Games: A Simulator Comparing Control Policies and Satellite Capability
entry.summary: Where Planning Changes the Outcome of Orbital Games arXiv · Oct 17, 2026The paper introduces OrbitalGym, a JAX-based simulation environment for adversarial orbital games in which teams of satellites maneuver during close-range encounters. The authors compare PD, LQR, model predictive path integral control, and Monte Carlo tree search across many capability configurations. They report that propellant ratio largely decides pursuit-evasion outcomes, while policy choice matters more in the lady-bandit-guard game.

entry.title: How exposure to instructions makes hidden rhetorical patterns in LLMs usable
entry.summary: From Geometry to Behavior: How Instruction Exposure Unlocks Latent Rhetorical Directions in LLMs arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This paper studies whether language models absorb analogy-based reasoning from pretraining and whether it can be activated at inference time. The authors extract an "Analogy Vector" from the residual stream and use it to steer explanation style across seven instruction-tuned models. They find the analogy direction exists in every base model, but how easily it can be behaviorally activated grows with the amount of instruction exposure during training.

entry.title: An Introduction to Large Language Models for Scientists and Professionals: a practical primer on how LLMs work, their limits, and how to use them responsibly.
entry.summary: An Introduction to Large Language Models for Scientists and Professionals arXiv · Oct 13, 2026This book is a practical introduction to large language models for scientists and professionals, based on lecture material from a master's course in artificial intelligence in medicine at the University of Turin. It explains core ideas such as tokenisation, embeddings, training, inference, context windows, prompting, and instruction hierarchies without mathematical detail. The text focuses on limitations including hallucinations, uncertainty, reproducibility, and bias, and on the need for verification and human oversight. It also covers privacy, governance, security, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and includes a hands-on exercise running a local model with Ollama and Open WebUI to query scientific papers, requiring no programming knowledge.

entry.title: Prompt-agnostic Language Models: Training Methods That Make LLMs Less Sensitive to Prompt Wording
entry.summary: Prompt-agnostic Language Models arXiv · Oct 13, 2026Large language models are highly sensitive to how prompts are phrased, and manual prompt tuning at inference time is costly and hard to scale. This paper instead studies train-time methods that build prompt robustness into instruction tuning. The authors introduce Prompt-TIES and Prompt-DARE, two gradient-merging methods that resolve interference among gradients from different paraphrases of the same prompt. Compared with other train-time approaches across four models, the methods reduce per-example variance nearly by half on fully fine-tuned models while costing little overall accuracy.

entry.title: Privacy-preserving release of ranked preference lists for aligning language models
entry.summary: Rank-Aware Differentially Private Release of Listwise Preferences for LLM Alignment arXiv · Oct 13, 2026This paper studies how to release listwise preference data for aligning large language models under local differential privacy. The full ranking space is highly sensitive and would require excessive noise, so the authors propose a rank-aware exponential mechanism that converts listwise data into a low-sensitivity fixed-size binary partition. The noise is concentrated near borderline items. Experiments on downstream LLM alignment tasks show it outperforms existing LDP baselines at matched privacy budgets.
